articles.title: 18F-FET PET for Detection of Recurrent Disease in Gliomas: Tips and Tricks for Interpretation.
articles.abstract: Gliomas are a heterogeneous group of primary brain tumors that are generally incurable. The current treatment paradigm for these tumors revolves around maximal safe resection and adjuvant chemoradiation; however, posttreatment changes can be difficult to distinguish from residual or recurrent disease. This makes it challenging to know whether treatments are working or the therapy should be escalated. Molecular imaging with amino acid PET has shown promise as a solution to this problem. The authors describe the interpretation considerations for the amino acid radiotracer fluorine 18-fluoroethyltyrosine (FET) in distinguishing posttreatment changes from recurrent glioma. The quantification of FET uptake on PET images and guidelines for interpretation are outlined.

articles.title: Beyond Metastatic Lymphadenopathy in Breast Cancer: Approach to Axillary Masses.
articles.abstract: The axilla is a pyramid-shaped space containing tissues of various origins including adipose, neural, vascular, cutaneous, myogenic, and lymphatic structures. Axillary masses are typically identified when patients present with palpable areas of concern or during imaging for breast cancer screening or staging. Breast imagers frequently encounter axillary masses while evaluating the axillary region at mammography and US. While reactive lymphadenopathy represents the most common cause of axillary lymph node enlargement, lymph node metastasis from breast cancer is a common cause of axillary masses requiring clinical evaluation. Recent immunization, particularly COVID-19 vaccination, is an important cause of unilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. Additional causes beyond metastatic lymphadenopathy must be considered in the differential diagnosis, including benign and malignant entities arising from accessory breast tissue, adipocytic, neurogenic, vascular, infectious, traumatic, and cutaneous origins. Understanding axillary anatomy is essential for developing a comprehensive differential diagnosis and determining appropriate management strategies. Systematic assessment of characteristic imaging and clinical findings, combined with thorough correlation with patient history and symptoms, enables accurate diagnosis. US serves as the primary imaging modality for mass assessment and biopsy guidance. Depending on the differential diagnosis, mammography, CT, and MRI provide supplementary information to better define mass origin and extent. Definitive diagnosis often requires histopathologic analysis. A systematic approach ensures accurate diagnosis and optimal management of axillary masses. © The Author(s), 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Subcutaneous and Visceral Adipose Tissue Reference Values from the Framingham Heart Study Thoracic and Abdominal CT: Erratum.
AI for reducing claims and compensation payments from missed fractures on radiographs.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the potential of BoneView, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for fracture detection on radiographs in claims cases related to missed fractures that resulted in financial compensation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter study included all patients who submitted a claim and received financial compensation for missed fractures on radiographs between January 2013 and December 2019 across the 38 university hospitals of the Greater Paris area (AP-HP-France). For each claimant, 5 control patients were selected from a contemporary single-center cohort of patients who underwent radiographs of the same anatomical regions (with or without fracture) performed in the emergency department of a university hospital, irrespective of fracture status. Three radiologists (musculoskeletal fellow, 5-year fellowship-trained radiologist, and > 20-year expert) independently performed blinded, unassisted, and AI-assisted interpretations following a 3-month washout. Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated with and without AI and for standalone AI. Compensation amounts were used to estimate potentially avoidable payouts. RESULTS: 156 patients (mean age, 42.2 years; 113 (72.4%) males), including 26 claimants with missed fractures on radiographs and 130 controls, were evaluated. 27/130 (20.8%) of the control cohort had fractures. Standalone AI sensitivity was 80.8% (21/26; 95% CI [60.7-93.5]) for claimants and 96.3% (26/27; 95% CI [81.0-99.9]) for the control cohort (p = 0.10). AI assistance did not significantly improve sensitivity, with expert reader sensitivity increasing from 81.1% to 92.5% (p = 0.10). Total compensation was €282,850 (€10,878 per case). AI-assisted detection could have potentially mitigated €265,314, representing a 93.8% theoretical reduction in institutional financial liability. CONCLUSION: AI-assisted fracture detection identified most missed fractures on radiographs leading to compensation and may help reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. KEY POINTS: Question Can AI-assisted fracture detection identify fractures missed by radiologists on radiographs that led to compensated medicolegal claims and institutional financial liability? Findings Standalone AI detected 21/26 (80.8%) of missed fractures in patients with compensated claims, corresponding to €265,314/€282,850 (93.8%) of total compensation in this cohort. Clinical relevance AI-assisted fracture detection can potentially increase radiologists' diagnostic accuracy and reduce medicolegal risk and compensation-related financial burden. Implementing AI tools in emergency settings may significantly mitigate patient harm and institutional costs associated with missed fractures.

articles.title: Deep learning-based segmentation of the ischemic core and severe hypodensity on noncontrast head CT compared with CT perfusion and diffusion-weighted imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the spatial overlap, imaging marker agreement, and outcome associations of acute ischemic regions of interest (ROIs) using deep-learning NCCT (DLNCCT) versus manual NCCT, CTP, and DWI-based segmentations. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We trained a deep learning model to segment ischemic ROIs on admission NCCT (DLNCCT). DLNCCT was compared with manual NCCT, CTP (rCBF < 30%/38%), and DWI using the Dice similarity coefficient (mean ± SD), Bland-Altman analysis (mean difference [95% CI]), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). For each ROI, we compared NCCT imaging biomarkers: average lesion density (HU); modified net water uptake (mNWU in %); total volume (mL); and hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volume (mL). DLNCCT biomarkers were associated with reversed 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (genOR [95% CI]). RESULTS: We used 218/762 train/test cases. Dice was 0.30 ± 0.30 between DLNCCT and manual segmentation, 0.22 ± 0.25 between DLNCCT-DWI, and 0.15 ± 0.22/0.21 ± 0.24 between CTP (rCBF < 30%/< 38%)-DWI. DLNCCT-DWI biomarker agreement was -1 HU (95% CI: -7; 6) for average density (CCC: 0.71), 4.9% (95% CI: -7.0; 16.8) for mNWU (CCC: 0.35), -16 mL (95% CI: -108; 76) for total volume (CCC: 0.57), and -4 mL (95% CI: -31; 23) for hypodense lesion volume (CCC: 0.75). Average lesion density (1.11 [95% CI: 1.06; 1.16]) and hypodense volume (0.85 [95% CI: 0.72; 0.99]) were associated with 90-day mRS. CONCLUSION: Spatial and biomarker agreement between DLNCCT and DWI was suboptimal but comparable to CTP-DWI. Nevertheless, DLNCCT-derived average lesion density and hypodense volume were associated with functional outcomes. KEY POINTS: Question Deep-learning models segment ischemic tissue on NCCT, but their spatial overlap and accuracy of imaging biomarker assessment relative to DWI and CTP core remain unclear. Findings Deep-learning NCCT segmentation showed good agreement with DWI in measuring hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volumes (- 4 mL [95% CI: -31; 23]; CCC 0.75). Clinical relevance Despite limited spatial overlap, NCCT-derived deep learning biomarkers showed agreement comparable to DWI, with improved performance in patients with poor ASPECTS and collateral scores. Hypodense volume and average lesion density were associated with functional outcome.

articles.title: PDGFRβ-Targeting VHH Tracer Enables Noninvasive PET Imaging of Kidney Fibrosis.
articles.abstract: With a prevalence above 10% worldwide, chronic kidney disease is one of the leading medical burdens. Independent of the underlying cause, kidney fibrosis emerges as the common final endpoint and serves as the most robust predictor of disease progression and long-term prognosis. Fibrosis is driven by extracellular matrix-producing mesenchymal cells, which are characterized by platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ) expression. PDGFRβ also mediates fibrogenesis in these cells and represents a potential therapeutic target for direct intervention or a potential anchor for selective delivery of antifibrotic drugs. Diagnostic approaches assessing PDGFRβ expression in kidneys are missing. Here, we developed and evaluated a novel tracer using a PDGFRβ-targeting biparatopic variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, designated SP02SP26-ABD, for in vivo, noninvasive, molecular imaging of kidney fibrosis. Methods: PDGFRβ expression was assessed in human kidney biopsies and publicly available transcriptomic datasets. In vivo imaging studies were performed in 2 distinct murine models of kidney fibrosis using fluorescence imaging and 89Zr-labeled PET. Specificity and dose dependency were evaluated using a nonspecific control variable domain of a heavy-chain-only antibody construct, R2R2-ABD, and coinjection of increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD. Ex vivo biodistribution and correlation with histologic and molecular markers of fibrosis were performed. Results: PDGFRβ was increased in fibrotic human kidneys across multiple disease entities, predominantly localized to pericytes and fibroblasts, supporting its relevance as a translational imaging target. In vivo imaging demonstrated significantly higher tracer accumulation in fibrotic compared with nonfibrotic kidneys across both models, whereas tracer accumulation in nonrenal organs was low, with minimal uptake in the spleen. We found no difference between fibrotic and nonfibrotic kidneys when using a nonspecific R2R2-ABD control construct, whereas increasing amounts of unlabeled SP02SP26-ABD led to a dose-dependent decrease in tracer accumulation, consistent with a saturation effect. Tracer signal correlated with PDGFRβ expression, confirming the specificity of the approach. Conclusion: We provide the first proof of concept for noninvasive PET imaging of PDGFRβ-expressing fibrogenic cells in kidney disease, supporting further development of this approach for specific, noninvasive assessment of kidney fibrosis.

articles.title: Clinical Study Protocol for PENTILULA: A Phase 1/2 Study Assessing [177Lu]Lu-Pentixather for Relapsed or Refractory CXCR4-Positive Acute Leukemia.
articles.abstract: C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4 (CXCR4) inhibition may represent a new therapeutic strategy for patients with acute leukemia (AL), not only by increasing chemosensitivity but also by preventing relapse through disruption of residual leukemic cell interactions with the bone marrow niche. Radiolabeled CXCR4 ligands are available for PET imaging ([68Ga]Ga-pentixafor) and radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) ([177Lu]Lu-pentixather/[90Y]Y-pentixather). Early clinical experience with CXCR4-targeted RPT, together with the reported feasibility of CXCR4-targeted PET in acute myeloid leukemia, supports the development of theranostic approaches targeting the CXCR4/C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12-defined leukemia-initiating cell niche. The objective of this study is to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of a single infusion of [177Lu]Lu-pentixather in patients with relapsed/refractory AL (including both acute myeloid leukemia and acute lymphoblastic leukemia). Methods: PENTILULA is an investigator-initiated, first-in-human, prospective phase 1/2 study based on a standard 3 + 3 dose-escalation design with 5 levels and 3-6 patients per level. Key inclusion criteria include patients with relapsed/refractory AL with CXCR4-positive leukemic cells. The primary endpoint is the incidence and evaluation of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and determination of the MTD. DLTs will be assessed 4-6 wk after RPT and include grade 3 or higher nonhematologic toxicity, prolonged grade 4 pancytopenia with hypocellular bone marrow, and excessive renal or hepatic radiation absorbed dose. The MTD is defined as the highest level at which fewer than one third of patients experience a DLT. In a subset of patients, [68Ga]Ga-pentixafor PET/MRI will be performed to explore the predictive value of theranostic PET imaging on CXCR4 expression, dosimetry, and treatment response. Conclusion: This first-in-human clinical study is ongoing, having reached the fifth and final activity level. [177Lu]Lu-pentixather is being used to definitively establish the MTD and preliminary efficacy of this CXCR4-targeted approach in this high-risk population with limited therapeutic options.

articles.title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor as a Radiotheranostic Target in Orthotopic Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a 5-y survival rate of approximately 20%. Although glypican-3-targeted radiotheranostics are under development, a plurality of patients with HCC lack glypican-3 expression, underscoring the need for alternative targetable antigens. Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is overexpressed in 50%-70% of HCC tumors and represents a clinically validated therapeutic target. Here, we developed and evaluated a panitumumab-based EGFR-targeted radiotheranostic pair, [89Zr]Zr-desferrioxamine-panitumumab ([89Zr]Zr-Pani) for immuno-PET and [225Ac]Ac-Macropa-panitumumab ([225Ac]Ac-Pani) for targeted α-particle therapy, in clinically relevant orthotopic HCC models. Methods: Panitumumab was conjugated with desferrioxamine or Macropa chelators and radiolabeled with 89Zr or 225Ac, respectively. EGFR expression was characterized across a panel of HCC cell lines. Binding affinity, biodistribution, and tumor specificity were assessed in subcutaneous and orthotopic Huh-7 models, with EGFR-mediated targeting confirmed by blocking (200-fold molar excess of unlabeled panitumumab). Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in mice bearing orthotopic Huh-7-Luc+ tumors (n = 6 per group) after a single 9.3 kBq dose of [225Ac]Ac-Pani, with longitudinal monitoring by bioluminescence imaging, [89Zr]Zr-Pani immuno-PET, and blood chemistry. Results: [89Zr]Zr-Pani exhibited high-affinity binding to EGFR (dissociation constant, 0.35 nM) and demonstrated robust tumor accumulation in both subcutaneous Huh-7 (20.6 ± 2.6 %IA/g) and orthotopic Huh-7-Luc+ tumors (19.3 ± 2.0 %IA/g) at 120-192 h postinjection. Biodistribution of [225Ac]Ac-Pani closely mirrored that of [89Zr]Zr-Pani across organs and tumors, with tumor uptake reduced approximately 5-fold by blocking (21.7 ± 1.1 vs. 4.5 ± 0.6 %IA/g; P < 0.0001), confirming EGFR-specific targeting. A single 9.3 kBq administration of [225Ac]Ac-Pani induced substantial early tumor regression and significantly prolonged median survival (70 d) compared with vehicle (28 d) and blocking (35 d) groups (log-rank P < 0.0001), with no clinically meaningful hepatotoxicity or renal toxicity. However, tumor regrowth eventually occurred in all treated mice. Conclusion: [89Zr]Zr-Pani and [225Ac]Ac-Pani represent a radiotheranostic pair that enables EGFR-specific imaging and targeted α-particle therapy in orthotopic HCC models. These findings establish EGFR as a promising radiotheranostic target in HCC, broadening the patient population eligible for image-guided radiopharmaceutical interventions for liver cancer.

articles.title: Patient Communication and Radiation Safety in [177Lu]Lu-PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy: International Survey of 102 Theranostic Centers.
articles.abstract: [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) is increasingly administered worldwide in both inpatient and outpatient settings. Despite its growing use, there is no harmonized international guidance on what patients should be told before, during, and after therapy. This study aimed to capture current clinical practice and expert opinion to identify areas of consensus and divergence to develop a patient information template. Methods: An international survey was conducted among theranostic centers performing [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT. The questionnaire covered pretreatment procedures, therapy procedures, radiation precautions guidance, and posttreatment procedures. Inpatient and outpatient settings were evaluated separately. Results: In total, 102 centers from 23 countries participated. High agreement was observed for most pretreatment procedures, core therapy aspects, and general posttreatment guidance. In contrast, substantial variability was identified in posttreatment radiation precautions, particularly regarding distancing measures, duration of precautions, transportation after discharge, household and hygiene recommendations, and guidance affecting social interactions. Conclusion: This international survey demonstrated broad consensus for core clinical procedures but showed variability in posttreatment radiation precautions after RPT. By summarizing current practice and translating it into a patient information template, this project supports more consistent patient guidance across diverse clinical settings.

articles.title: Preclinical Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Modeling of PSMA Radioligands: Demonstrating Nonspecific Retention and Reversible Albumin-Binding Effects.
articles.abstract: Radiopharmaceutical therapy with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) radioligands has emerged as a promising treatment modality for metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling has been applied in clinical studies of PSMA radioligands. However, clinical models are necessarily simplified because of sparse patient data, which may mask important pharmacokinetic processes. The aim of this study was to perform PBPK modeling on comprehensive preclinical data and identify previously neglected dynamics of PSMA radioligands with translation relevance. Methods: Biodistribution and albumin-binding affinity data were previously obtained for the 2 PSMA radioligands [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 and [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T and the 3 albumin-binding PSMA radioligands [177Lu]Lu-SibuDAB, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-ALB-53, and [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-ALB-56. A baseline, preclinical PBPK model was built using a widely studied radioligand PBPK model structure. Three types of modifications to the baseline model were developed: nonspecific retention in PSMA-negative tissues and kidneys, change from an irreversible to a reversible albumin-binding model, and albumin-bound fraction implementation. Models with modification combinations were built, and regressions were performed against the biodistribution data. The modifications were evaluated on the regression performances, and simulations of the fitted models were compared with clinically established baseline regressions through time-integrated activity (TIA) ratios. Results: For all radioligands, incorporating nonspecific retention markedly improved the corrected Akaike information criterion (AIC). The reversible albumin-binding model showed improved AIC for all albumin-binding radioligands. The implementation of albumin-bound fractions degraded the AIC but showed minor impact on fits. With nonspecific retention, substantial increases in TIAs were observed for PSMA-negative organs, particularly for the dose-limited organ red marrow where TIA ratios reached 3.0, 1.5, and 1.6 for [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617, [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T, and [177Lu]Lu-SibuDAB, respectively. TIAs for PSMA-positive tissues and kidneys remained relatively stable. Conclusion: This preclinical study demonstrated that disregarding nonspecific retention led to marked underestimation of doses to PSMA-negative tissues such as in the radiosensitive red marrow. The models with reversible albumin-binding further improved the regressions for the albumin-binding radioligands but had limited impact on TIA estimates. By integrating these mechanisms, preclinical PBPK models provide novel insights into radioligand kinetics and can inform the refinement of clinical PBPK models toward safer and more individualized PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: Complications after Spine Surgery: Updated Imaging Concepts and Structured Classification Approach.
Saline tract sealing to reduce pneumothorax rates following CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Pneumothorax remains the most common complication following CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy, increasing morbidity and healthcare utilisation. Saline tract sealing has been proposed as a simple technique to reduce the risk of pneumothorax, but its effectiveness remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched for studies evaluating saline tract sealing following CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model for pneumothorax and chest drain insertion. RESULTS: The search identified 151 articles, of which 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. Ten studies (one randomised controlled trial and nine observational studies) comprising 2252 patients compared saline tract sealing with no sealant and were included in the meta-analysis. One study used an alternative sealant comparator and was synthesised narratively. Saline tract sealing was associated with a significant reduction in pneumothorax (RR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.42-0.80; I² = 82%) and chest drain insertion (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.15-0.61; I² = 55%). These findings remained robust on sensitivity analysis excluding studies incorporating rapid patient rollover as a co-intervention, with persistent reductions in pneumothorax (RR 0.51, 95% CI: 0.33-0.78) and chest drain insertion (RR 0.31, 95% CI: 0.13-0.75). CONCLUSION: Saline tract sealing may be an effective and practical strategy to reduce the incidence of pneumothorax and chest drain insertion after CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy. Given the very low certainty of the current evidence, further randomised controlled trials are required to confirm these findings. KEY POINTS: Question Does saline tract sealing reduce rates of pneumothorax and chest drain insertion following CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy? Findings Saline tract sealant was associated with reduced rates of pneumothorax and chest drain insertion following CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy compared with no sealant. Clinical relevance Saline tract sealing is a simple, low-cost technique that can be readily implemented to improve the safety of CT-guided percutaneous lung biopsy.

articles.title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) for detecting haemodynamically significant coronary disease in patients with anatomically long-segment lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and invasive pressure-wire FFR within 30 days. Anatomically long-segment disease was defined as lesion length ≥ 20 mm. Invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 was the reference standard. CT-FFR was assessed at vessel and patient levels, with patient-level CT-FFR defined as the minimum value per patient and patient-level disease as any invasive FFR ≤ 0.80. Diagnostic discrimination, threshold-based classification, and Bland-Altman agreement were evaluated. RESULTS: The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant. CONCLUSION: CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment. KEY POINTS: Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Longitudinal MRI-based Delta-Habitat model for predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a machine learning model integrating habitat imaging features before and after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) to predict pathological complete response (pCR) to NACI in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). METHODS: A multicenter retrospective study was conducted involving 520 HNSCC patients who received NACI across three hospitals. Unlike conventional Delta-Radiomics, we developed Delta-Habitat model that integrates Pre-NACI and Post-NACI MRI spatial habitat radiomics features, and dynamically learns task-specific contributions from each timepoint. Predictive performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to quantify the contribution of individual features to model predictions. We assessed and compared the diagnostic performance of senior and junior radiologists, both with and without the aid of the Delta-Habitat model. RESULTS: Delta-Habitat model outperformed Pre-NACI feature-based models and traditional radiomics-based Delta-Rad model, with AUC of 0.828, 0.825 and 0.813 in validation and two external test cohorts respectively. Post-treatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (Post-NLR) was identified as an independent predictor of pCR. Integrating Delta-Radiomics and clinical features into Delta-Habitat model did not yield a significant improvement in predictive performance, the combined model showed slightly improved AUC over Delta-Habitat alone, reaching 0.877 (train), 0.834 (val), 0.837 (test1), and 0.834 (test2). SHAP analysis revealed that Post-NACI features contributed more substantially to model predictions than Pre-NACI features. The Delta-Habitat model consistently exhibited better performance than radiologists in comparative evaluations. Moreover, senior and junior radiologists both showed increases in AUC values with the assistance of the Delta-Habitat model, by 0.073 and 0.177 respectively on the internal validation cohort and by 0.087 and 0.142 on the external test cohort. CONCLUSIONS: The longitudinal MRI-based habitat model can provide valuable information for predicting the response to NACI in HNSCC and enhance radiologists' diagnostic performance.

articles.title: ESR Bridges: mesenteric ischaemia: new developments in imaging and treatment-a multidisciplinary view.
Sports-related peripheral neuropathies in athletes: mechanisms, imaging evaluation, and sport-specific patterns.
articles.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy in athletes is increasingly recognized as a significant source of morbidity, with injury patterns varying according to the biomechanical demands of specific sports. Although peripheral nerve disorders in athletes may result from acute trauma, they more commonly arise from chronic, repetitive mechanical stress inherent to athletic activity. Despite their frequency, they frequently remain underdiagnosed, as clinical manifestations often overlap with other musculoskeletal disorders. Mechanisms of injury include compression, traction, laceration, ischemia, and repetitive microtrauma. Distinct athletic modalities are associated with characteristic neuropathies reflecting sport-specific kinematics and loading patterns. Awareness of these biomechanical factors and recognition of typical clinical presentations are essential for accurate assessment of athletes with suspected nerve injury. Diagnostic evaluation frequently requires advanced imaging modalities, particularly magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) and high-resolution ultrasound (HRUS), which enable detailed structural assessment of peripheral nerves and detection of secondary imaging findings. Electrodiagnostic studies may provide complementary functional information in selected cases. Early and precise diagnosis is critical to guide management, facilitate safe return to sport, and prevent long-term functional deficits. While most nerve disorders respond to conservative treatment, severe, progressive, or refractory cases may warrant surgical intervention to restore function and enable return to play (RTP). This review examines mechanisms of injury, clinical evaluation, classification systems, imaging findings, and sport-specific patterns of peripheral nerve injury across diverse athletic disciplines.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ Inclusion in Medical Imaging Practice: A Scoping Review of Barriers, Impacts, and Strategies.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Medical imaging encounters are shaped by structured workflows, documentation systems, and clinical assumptions about sex, gender, anatomy, and relationships. This scoping review mapped published literature on LGBTQ+ inclusion in medical imaging practice, focusing on how gender and sexuality norms are represented across imaging workflows, environments, professional culture, and education, and what is known about related barriers, impacts, and strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, Scopus, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched using a Population-Concept-Context framework. Eligible sources addressed heteronormativity, cisnormativity, or LGBTQ+ inclusion within medical imaging settings. Data were charted by study characteristics, imaging context, population focus, and primary study focus, then synthesized descriptively and narratively. RESULTS: Forty-six sources were included. Most were published from 2021 onward and were concentrated in the United States. Evidence was weighted toward transgender and gender-diverse populations, with limited literature addressing sexuality-diverse populations, nonbinary-specific experiences, modality-specific practice, or LGBTQ+ staff inclusion. Reported barriers included binary information systems, gendered screening, misgendering, gendered reporting language, gendered environments, and limited modality guidance. Reported impacts included distress, reduced trust, disclosure burden, reduced engagement with care, and risk of inappropriate or inaccurate imaging pathways. Strategies focused on inclusive documentation, anatomy-informed screening, affirming communication, trauma-informed care, staff education, policy, and audit, but were rarely evaluated. CONCLUSION: LGBTQ+ inclusion in medical imaging is central to safe, accurate, and equitable practice. Future work should move beyond recommending inclusive practice toward implementing and evaluating changes to information systems, clinical practices, and communication.

articles.title: Beyond Physical Displacement: Standardization of Breast Biopsy Markers, Multimodal Stratification, and Academic Training Challenges.
Fetal and perinatal neuroimaging of midbrain and hindbrain malformations.
articles.abstract: Midbrain and hindbrain malformations comprise a heterogeneous group of developmental disorders with overlapping clinical and imaging features that can pose diagnostic challenges in the fetal and perinatal periods. While some of these malformations are associated with favorable outcomes, others are indicative of poor viability. Accurate and comprehensive imaging evaluation is critical to guide prognostication and optimize perinatal management. This pictorial review illustrates the prenatal and postnatal imaging spectrum of these uncommon disorders and highlights characteristic findings that facilitate diagnosis and differentiation. Representative cases include diencephalic-mesencephalic junction dysplasia, Möbius sequence, rhombencephalosynapsis, microcephaly with disproportionate cerebellar and brainstem hypoplasia syndrome, Walker-Warburg syndrome, Joubert syndrome-related disorders, horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis, pontine tegmental cap dysplasia, medullary malformations, pontocerebellar hypoplasia, and cerebellar hemisphere hypoplasia, organized based on a previously proposed classification system.

articles.title: Evaluating the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence for pediatric appendicular fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric fracture detection on plain radiographs can be challenging, and missed fractures can have important clinical consequences. Artificial intelligence has been increasingly investigated as a tool to support fracture detection in children. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence models for detecting appendicular fractures on pediatric radiographs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted from inception through February 1, 2026. Studies evaluating AI models for detecting appendicular fractures in pediatric populations using plain radiographs were included. Pooled sensitivities and specificities were calculated using bivariate random-effects meta-analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed based on anatomical site, unit of analysis, and comparator type. RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity for standalone AI models were 92.0% (95% CI, 90.4-93.4%) and 87.9% (95% CI, 84.5-90.6%), respectively, with an hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) area under the curve of 0.96. Considerable heterogeneity was observed (I2, 49-78%). No significant differences were found between per-image and per-patient analyses (P=0.78). Differences in diagnostic performance among physicians using AI models, standalone AI models, and physicians without AI models were not significant (P=0.20). Fagan nomogram analysis demonstrated that at 50% pre-test probability, a positive AI result increased post-test probability to 90%, while a negative result reduced it to 7%. CONCLUSION: AI models demonstrate considerable diagnostic accuracy for detecting pediatric appendicular fractures on radiography. Considerable heterogeneity and concerns regarding real-life implementation highlight the need for prospective studies with standardized methodologies.

articles.title: Imaging of Isocitrate Dehydrogenase-Mutant Gliomas in the Era of Isocitrate Dehydrogenase Inhibitors: What Radiologists Need to Know.
articles.abstract: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas, including IDH-mutant astrocytomas and IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendrogliomas, exhibit biologically distinct behaviors from IDH-wildtype glioblastomas, showing better survival outcomes and requiring different treatment strategies. The recent FDA approval of vorasidenib, an IDH mutation inhibitor, has introduced a paradigm shift in the treatment of IDH-mutant gliomas and has focused attention to the role of imaging information in the routine clinical management of these tumors. In this review, we provide an overview of the clinical fundamentals of IDH-mutant gliomas and highlight the preoperative and postoperative imaging features of these lesions, which are important for radiologists to recognize and communicate with clinicians.

articles.title: Noninvasive Diagnosis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Outside Guideline-Defined High-Risk Populations: Evolving Perspectives in the Era of MASLD.
articles.abstract: Noninvasive imaging-based diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in high-risk patients currently relies on the radiological hallmark of arterial-phase hyperenhancement followed by delayed washout. These criteria were designed to achieve both a high positive predictive value and sufficient specificity when applied to well-defined target populations. However, the incidence of HCC is rising globally among individuals outside the traditional high-risk groups, including those with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly known as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease) and genetic predispositions. This shifting epidemiology poses challenges to the current noninvasive diagnostic strategies and the binary classification of patients as either "at high-risk" or "not at high-risk," which heavily depends on established risk factors such as chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and liver cirrhosis. Consequently, HCC in non-high-risk individuals is often diagnosed at more advanced stages, underscoring the urgent need for reliable and noninvasive diagnostic tools tailored to this demographic population. These challenges present opportunities for the radiology community to play a proactive role in addressing them. Given the heterogeneous risk factors among low- and intermediate-risk populations, integrated strategies incorporating imaging features, fibrosis stage, serum biomarkers, individualized risk models, and artificial intelligence-assisted cross-sectional imaging may help improve the noninvasive diagnosis of non-cirrhotic or metabolically driven HCC. This review summarizes the current performance and limitations of noninvasive diagnosis outside the conventional high-risk populations in the era of MASLD and highlights emerging diagnostic strategies that warrant further investigation as evidence continues to accumulate.

articles.title: Fetal Liver Volume and Morphology in Growth-Restricted Fetuses and Their Association With Neonatal Morbidity: An MRI Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) may induce redistribution of the fetal circulation to preserve perfusion of vital organs. Reduced hepatic delivery of oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood may cause volumetric and morphological remodeling. PURPOSE: To quantify fetal liver volume and morphology in FGR and assess associations with adverse neonatal outcomes. STUDY TYPE: Single-center, prospective and retrospective. POPULATION: Ninety-two singleton pregnancies: 36 FGR cases (prospective) and 56 appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) controls (retrospective). FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3-T, True Fast Imaging with Steady-State Free Precession (TrueFISP) for fetal liver and body imaging, and TrueFISP or Half-Fourier Acquisition Single-shot Turbo Spin-Echo for brain imaging. ASSESSMENT: The fetal liver, body, and brain were segmented using deep learning tools. Liver volume, liver-to-body and brain-to-liver volume ratios, and 12 liver PyRadiomics shape features were assessed. Neonates were followed for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (CANO) until discharge. STATISTICAL TESTS: Linear regression assessed associations with gestational age in AGA fetuses. Linear mixed-effects models compared groups, adjusting for gestational age and fetal sex. Univariable logistic regression assessed associations with CANO. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate at 0.05. RESULTS: FGR fetuses had significantly lower liver volume than AGA fetuses (74.95 ± 1.76 vs. 114.89 ± 2.18 cm3), lower liver-to-body ratio (0.053 ± 0.001 vs. 0.057 ± 0.001), and higher brain-to-liver ratio (2.637 ± 0.085 vs. 1.978 ± 0.047). FGR fetuses demonstrated significantly less elongated liver geometry, (10.7% higher PyRadiomics elongation values) and had a significantly higher surface-to-volume ratio (11.9%). CANO occurred in 30/92 neonates (27 FGR, 3 AGA). Higher brain-to-liver ratio (OR = 4.12, 95% CI: 1.93-8.77), PyRadiomics elongation values (less elongated geometry; OR = 2.04, 95% CI: 1.26-3.30), PyRadiomics flatness values (less flattened geometry; OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.07-2.65), and surface-to-volume ratio (OR = 3.26, 95% CI: 1.80-5.90) were significantly associated with CANO. DATA CONCLUSION: FGR was associated with reduced fetal liver size and altered geometry, which were associated with neonatal morbidity. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: 2.

articles.title: Cervicocerebral angiography in trauma using split-bolus whole-body CT - comparison with dedicated neuroradiological CT angiography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine whether split-bolus whole-body computed tomography (WBCT) provides sufficient cervicocerebral arterial opacification and diagnostic evaluability for vascular assessment in polytrauma compared with dedicated neuroradiological computed tomography angiography (CTA). METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study, 130 polytrauma patients undergoing split-bolus WBCT were age- and sex-matched to 130 patients undergoing dedicated head-and-neck CTA between January 2023 and June 2025. Arterial attenuation was measured in 15 cervicocerebral segments. Adequate vessel opacification was defined as ≥ 250 HU. Five radiologists independently assessed arterial contrast, venous contamination, overall image quality, and diagnostic evaluability. Statistical analysis included unpaired t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Fisher's exact tests with multiple-comparison correction. RESULTS: 260 patients were included (mean age 56.3 ± 24 years; 90 female). Dedicated CTA demonstrated significantly higher attenuation in all segments except the cervical internal carotid artery (ICA) (p = 0.08). Mean and median attenuation exceeded 250 HU in all segments for both protocols. Measurements <250 HU were more frequent with split-bolus WBCT, reaching significance only in the petrous ICA (p = 0.02). Subjectively, dedicated CTA showed higher arterial contrast and less venous contamination (both p < 0.01), whereas overall image quality varied across readers. Diagnostic evaluability was high in both cohorts, with no significant differences in four of five readers. CONCLUSIONS: Despite lower arterial enhancement, split-bolus WBCT provided adequate cervicocerebral arterial opacification and high diagnostic evaluability, supporting feasibility for initial vascular assessment in polytrauma. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: The findings support the feasibility of split-bolus WBCT for initial cervicocerebral vascular assessment in polytrauma patients.

articles.title: Quantitative Hepatobiliary MRI for Early Prognostic Assessment After Liver Transplantation: Survival Prediction Using the Contrast Enhancement Index.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility and prognostic value of the contrast enhancement index (CEI) derived from gadobenate dimeglumine (Gd-BOPTA)-enhanced hepatobiliary-phase (HBP) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for early assessment of liver graft function after liver transplantation (LT). METHODS: This retrospective study included LT recipients undergoing Gd-BOPTA-enhanced MRI within 6 months after transplantation. CEI was calculated using liver-to-psoas signal intensity ratios on pre-contrast and HBP images acquired 90-120 minutes after contrast administration. ROC, Kaplan-Meier, and age-adjusted Cox regression analyses evaluated associations with mortality. RESULTS: Seventy patients (median age, 62 years; interquartile range [IQR], 48-74) were included. CEI was quantifiable in all cases (median, 1.27; IQR, 1.09-1.37). Non-survivors had significantly lower CEI values than survivors (median, 1.17 vs 1.31; p = 0.03; Cliff's δ = -0.28). ROC analysis showed moderate discrimination for mortality (AUC, 0.667; 95% CI, 0.529-0.793), with an optimal cutoff of 1.301 (sensitivity, 88%; specificity, 51.2%). Patients with CEI <1.301 had significantly lower overall survival (log-rank p = 0.028). After adjustment for recipient age, CEI remained associated with mortality (HR per 0.1-unit increase, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.64-0.98; p = 0.035). CONCLUSION: Quantitative CEI measurement on Gd-BOPTA HBP MRI is feasible after LT, and lower CEI values. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This study links quantitative Gd-BOPTA-enhanced HBP MRI with overall survival after LT, supporting CEI as a potential non-invasive imaging biomarker for postoperative risk stratification.

articles.title: Spectral-habitat analysis and perfusion fingerprinting on contrast-enhanced ultrasound for characterizing tumor perfusion in breast lesions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop a short-time Fourier transform (STFT)-based perfusion fingerprinting method combined with spectral-habitat analysis for characterizing pixel-wise perfusion heterogeneity on contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) and to evaluate its ability to differentiate benign and malignant breast lesions. METHODS: Pixel-wise CEUS time-series data were transformed into the time-frequency domain using STFT. Principal component analysis (PCA) was then applied to reduce the dimensionality of STFT-derived features and generate perfusion fingerprinting maps that preserved spatial and temporal perfusion information. Spectral-habitat maps were generated using K-means clustering to identify perfusion-related tumor subregions. A triple-branch multi-layer fusion model was constructed to integrate full-region and habitat-derived features for lesion classification. To provide an exploratory conventional CEUS quantitative baseline, TIC-derived perfusion features were additionally extracted and evaluated using machine learning classifiers. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, decision curve analysis (DCA), and confusion matrix. RESULTS: The proposed STFT-based perfusion fingerprinting method enabled a more comprehensive characterization of tumor perfusion heterogeneity by preserving pixel-wise spatiotemporal dynamics of CEUS signals. CEUS-derived spectral-habitat maps provided visual representations of intratumoral perfusion heterogeneity and improved the interpretability of the model outputs. In this cohort, the triple-branch multi-layer fusion model achieved an AUC of 0.953, with accuracy of 0.909, precision of 0.907, recall of 0.925, and F1 score of 0.912. Exploratory TIC-based conventional CEUS models achieved AUCs ranging from 0.7677 to 0.8186. DCA suggested potential clinical utility of the proposed model across a range of threshold probabilities, and confusion matrix analysis showed favorable classification performance. CONCLUSION: The STFT-based perfusion fingerprinting method combined with spectral-habitat analysis provides a promising CEUS-based framework for characterizing perfusion heterogeneity in breast lesions. By preserving pixel-wise spatiotemporal information, this approach may provide complementary quantitative information for more interpretable differentiation between benign and malignant lesions.

articles.title: CT-guided biopsy of pulmonary ground-glass nodules: core-needle biopsy versus fine-needle aspiration.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the diagnostic performance and complication profiles of CT-guided core-needle biopsy (CNB) and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) for pulmonary ground-glass nodules (GGNs). METHODS: Consecutive patients who underwent CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of pulmonary GGNs between January 2021 and August 2022 were screened. Of 657 patients assessed, 538 were included (CNB, n = 448; FNA, n = 90). Six FNA results classified as atypical cells were considered indeterminate and excluded from binary diagnostic-performance analyses, leaving 532 classifiable cases. Final diagnoses were established by surgical pathology or imaging follow-up of at least 12 months. Diagnostic performance was compared without adjustment, whereas complication outcomes were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). RESULTS: Among the 532 classifiable biopsies, the overall accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were 93.2%, 91.4%, and 100.0%, respectively, based on the available composite reference standard. CNB showed higher unadjusted accuracy than FNA (94.6% vs. 85.7%, P = 0.007) and higher sensitivity (93.2% vs. 82.4%, P = 0.008). In the full cohort of 538 procedures, multivariable analysis showed that CNB was associated with higher odds of intrapulmonary hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.91; P < 0.001) and hemoptysis (aOR: 3.07; P < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant association was observed for pneumothorax. CONCLUSION: CT-guided percutaneous biopsy yielded determinate diagnostic results for most pulmonary GGNs under the available composite reference standard. In unadjusted comparisons, CNB showed higher diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity than FNA but was associated with greater risks of hemorrhagic complications. Given the lack of adjustment for baseline differences in diagnostic-performance analyses, the apparent diagnostic advantage of CNB should be interpreted cautiously. Biopsy technique should be individualized according to lesion characteristics and patient-specific risks.

articles.title: Clinical-MRI-IVIM combined model for differentiating thymic epithelial tumors from anterior mediastinal lymphoma in large masses.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic value of clinical and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) parameters for differentiating large anterior mediastinal invasive masses (≥ 3 cm), particularly thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) and lymphomas. METHODS: This prospective study included 92 patients (mean age, 44.8 ± 15.5 years) with pathologically confirmed TETs (n = 52) or lymphomas (n = 40) who underwent routine MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging, and IVIM sequences. Quantitative parameters, including the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), true diffusion coefficient (D), pseudo-diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction (f), were measured. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to construct predictive models. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with area under the curve (AUC) compared by the DeLong test. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling, and multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors. RESULTS: Compared with TET, lymphoma was associated with younger age, higher female proportion, higher LDH, larger volume, more frequent pleural and/or lung invasion, and higher D * values (all p < 0.05). Age, sex, LDH level, lung and/or pleural infiltration, and f in the IVIM model were risk predictive factors for distinguishing lymphoma from TET. Among all models, the clinical MRI-IVM model achieved the highest diagnostic performance numerically (AUC = 0.946, 95% CI: 0.901-0.991); However, compared with the clinical MRI model (AUC = 0.929, 95% CI: 0.873-0.985), the increment brought by adding IVIM parameters was not significant (DeLong test, P = 0.316). Calibration analysis showed good consistency between predicted probabilities. The apparent AUC of Bootstrap's internal validation was 0.946, the estimation deviation was 0.017, and the standard error was 0.022, indicating limited optimism in the model's performance. CONCLUSIONS: The clinical-MRI-IVIM model had shown relatively good diagnostic performance in preoperative differentiation of large anterior mediastinal TETs and lymphoma. However, there is no statistical difference in the increment benefit generated by IVIM parameters in the composite model. Therefore, in order to elucidate the clinical efficacy of IVIM, further large-scale, prospective, and multi-center studies are necessary.

articles.title: Combined Metasurface and Metamaterial Passive Transmit Lens and Receive Array for 3 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Metasurfaces (MSs) and metamaterials (MMs) can reduce transmit field nulls caused by wavelength effects at higher MR field strengths. We present a layered MM and MS resonant structure that improves transmit field performance when used as a combined slab (i.e., the metaslab), while also operating as a receive array. METHODS: The MS structure consists of cross-shaped traces joined by capacitors on a PCB. It is embedded between two layers of a MM consisting of inductively coupled longitudinal strips acting as a 2D transmission line. The two structures are intrinsically decoupled and support connection ports to create an 8-element receive array. Simulations were performed with a realistic body phantom, and imaging experiments were performed at 3 T on a large water phantom and in vivo on an adult male's abdomen. RESULTS: Transmit efficiency is improved by a factor of 1.45 in simulation over body coil alone using a realistic body model and by a factor of 1.55 from in vivo measurement. Inhomogeneity is reduced from 24.1% to 17.5% in simulation with realistic human body models, and from 18.5% to 13.9% in phantom measurements. Furthermore, the SAR efficiency is improved by 26% in simulation. In receive, the measured SNR is improved by a factor of 1.48 at the center, compared to a 1.76 improvement with equivalent channel count conventional surface coil array. CONCLUSION: The proposed combination of MS and MM operating dually as a passive field lens and receive array improves homogeneity, SAR efficiency, and receive sensitivity for 3 T abdominal MRI.

articles.title: Long-term trends and projections of CT and MRI utilization across selected OECD countries: a framework for sustainable imaging service planning.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: CT and MRI utilization is increasing across high-income countries, partly because of population ageing. This study integrated cross-country trends in examination rates, demographic change, and scanner productivity across OECD countries to project utilization to 2050 and inform sustainable service planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: CT and MRI examination rates were obtained from the OECD Data Explorer and Japan's National Database of Health Insurance Claims Open Data. Population data were derived from the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024. Linear regression projected examination rates to 2050. Pearson coefficients assessed associations between imaging rates and population shares aged 0-14, 15-64, and ≥ 65 years. Scanner productivity was calculated as annual examinations per device. RESULTS: CT utilization was strongly associated with the population aged ≥ 65 years in all countries (r = 0.95-1.00). MRI showed similarly strong associations in most countries (r = 0.95-0.99), with Italy as the main exception. Linear extrapolation projected CT rates of approximately 722 examinations per 1000 population in Korea and 520 in the United States by 2050, while MRI rates reached approximately 327 in France and 308 in Germany. Population-level utilization did not consistently correspond to device-level productivity; CT examinations per scanner ranged from 2153.3 in Japan to 11,526.5 in Canada. CONCLUSIONS: Population ageing was associated with increasing CT and MRI utilization. Future demand may also depend on health system organization and scanner productivity. Sustainable planning should integrate demographic forecasting, appropriateness stewardship, operational optimization, workforce development, and technological innovation rather than rely solely on proportional capacity expansion. KEY POINTS: Question Ageing drives CT/MRI demand (r = 0.95-1.00 for CT); projected to continue to 2050, offering a valuable planning window. Findings High utilization ≠ high scanner productivity; operational organization shapes imaging output independently of demand volume. Critical relevance statement Sustainable planning requires demographic forecasting, appropriateness management, and technological innovation, not just capacity expansion.

articles.title: A Fully Automated Segment-Specific CCTA Plaque Quantification Workflow using Deep Learning.
articles.abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) remains essential for diagnosing coronary artery disease, while the focus has moved from stenosis to plaque burden. Current workflows either need manual adjustments that limit consistency and efficiency, or they lack segment-specific precision. This study evaluated the effectiveness and reliability of a fully automated deep learning-based plaque quantification method using CCTA. DVPlaque workflow, a fully automated deep learning model, was developed to quantify segment-specific plaque volume. A total of 271 CCTA scans were included. Plaque quantification was performed by the expert and DVPlaque model, respectively. Reliability was measured through interclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis and Bland-Altman plots. DVPlaque workflow cost less time than expert measurement (p < 0.0001). Among these segments of major coronary arteries, proximal left ascending artery (LAD) had the highest prevalence of plaque (97.0%). Among these coronary arteries, the volumes of total plaque (TP), calcified plaque (CP), noncalcified plaque (NCP), and low-density NCP were the highest in LAD (all p-values < 0.05). On a per-patient level, the ICCs for TP, CP, and NCP volume were 0.962, 0.985, and 0.932. The corresponding biases and 95% limits of agreement were - 25.39 [ - 261.51, 210.73] mm3, 11.88 [ - 52.78, 76.55] mm3, and - 37.27 [ - 255.88, 181.33] mm3. For TP, CP, and NCP, per-vessel ICCs were all > 0.90, and per-segment ICCs were > 0.90 except for mid-LAD NCP (0.887). DVPlaque scheme was capable of quantifying plaque volume with excellent efficiency. The automated quantification of CP and NCP exhibited strong reliability even on a per-segment level, facilitating clinical application.

articles.title: Nondisease Sources of Radiomic Texture Variation on Plain Radiographs: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Anatomical Region, Projection, and Resolution in a Public Fracture Archive.
articles.abstract: Radiomic texture features from plain radiographs feed machine learning models on the assumption that they reflect tissue rather than anatomy or acquisition. In a public multihospital fracture archive, we quantified how anatomical region and radiographic projection, each adjusted for the other and for image resolution, shift 17 radiomic features, how much feature variance resolution explains, and a bony superimposition contrast defined within region. This retrospective cross-sectional secondary analysis used FracAtlas (4083 musculoskeletal radiographs from three hospitals); 4024 images were analyzed. For each z-scored feature (10 first-order, 7 Gy-level co-occurrence matrix [GLCM]), linear models estimated adjusted differences (β, SD units), and resolution by variance explained (R2), with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction within each factor. Superimposition (hip and shoulder vs hand and leg; n = 3630), a grouping of regions, was analyzed as a pooled regional contrast rather than an independent factor. Region shifted 16 of 17 features (radiomic uniformity, hand vs leg - 0.66 SD [95% CI - 0.72 to - 0.59]). Resolution explained up to 16.8% of single-feature variance and changed the fracture log-odds coefficient by more than 15% for 7 of 10 interpretable features. Projection had the smallest effects (radiomic 10th percentile, lateral vs frontal - 0.32 SD). The superimposition contrast produced the largest shifts (GLCM energy - 2.26 SD [95% CI - 2.36 to - 2.16]). Radiomic texture on plain radiographs varies substantially with anatomy and acquisition, independently of fracture status. Radiograph radiomics studies should record and adjust for region, projection, and resolution, report region-specific estimates, and validate across sites.

articles.title: AI-Based Low-Dose Chest CT Assessment of Coronary Artery Calcification Score: An Analysis of Accuracy-Relating Factors.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the accuracy of AI-based coronary artery calcium scoring on nongated low-dose chest CT and identifies factors affecting calcium risk classification, using ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT as the reference standard. This prospective study included 312 patients with chest pain who underwent ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT and additional low-dose chest CT (LDCT). LDCT images were reconstructed using pulmonary and standard kernels. AI software automatically quantified Agatston, mass, volume, and total coronary artery calcium scores (CACSs). Patients were stratified by Agatston-based risk category, heart rate (≤ 65 vs. > 65 bpm), and BMI (< 25 vs. ≥ 25 kg/m2). Agreement, systematic bias, and risk classification performance were assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, ICC analysis, Friedman tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, linear regression, and confusion matrices. Pulmonary kernel LDCT produced Agatston scores comparable to ECG-gated CT, with no significant differences across heart rate, BMI, or calcium severity subgroups. Under this kernel, measurement bias showed weak but significant correlations with heart rate and BMI (r = 0.145 and r = 0.131, respectively; both P < 0.05). Overall, nongated LDCT-derived CACS correlated strongly with reference CACS (r > 0.94). The low heart rate/low-BMI subgroup showed the best risk stratification performance, with 80% accuracy and good agreement (κ = 0.72). AI-assisted CACS assessment on nongated low-dose chest CT may serve as an adjunctive tool for opportunistic coronary artery calcification screening and preliminary cardiovascular risk stratification. Its accuracy may be influenced by reconstruction kernel and calcification burden, whereas heart rate and BMI may not be significant influencing factors.Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100073,2 April 2025, the study was retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Cross-Center Stroke Evaluation using Carotid Ultrasound Patterns via Scale-Adaptive Frequency-Enhanced Neural Network.
articles.abstract: Medical imaging datasets vary across institutions due to differences in scanner types, posing challenges for model generalization. To address the issue, this study proposed a scale-adaptive frequency-enhanced neural network (SAFE-Net), which leveraged a DWT-ViT encoder to incorporate frequency-domain features into a transformer-based architecture for cross-center stroke evaluation. The discrete wavelet transform (DWT) decomposed carotid color Doppler (CCD) images into multiresolution frequency sub-bands. The extracted high-resolution (Xh) and low-resolution (Xl) features are concatenated to enhance both local and global feature extraction. Experimental results demonstrated that SAFE-Net achieves the highest accuracy, with 92.5% accuracy on Institution A and 93.75% on Institution B, outperforming other models in stroke evaluation. SAFE-Net maintains cross-center generalization, with an accuracy of 90.73% when trained on Institution A and tested on Institution B, and 89.16% in the reverse setting. Also, the model required 25% fewer parameters and 2.0× fewer FLOPs than conventional models. These findings underscored the effectiveness of SAFE-Net across diverse medical imaging datasets.

articles.title: ParetoRx: A Multiobjective Radiogenomic Framework Integrating Pareto Optimization and Q-Learning for Exploratory Compound Prioritization in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: Imaging-defined high-risk phenotypes may capture biologically aggressive disease states, but translating them into therapeutic hypotheses remains challenging. We developed ParetoRx, a radiogenomic imaging-informatics framework integrating computed tomography radiomics, pathway-level transcriptomic analysis, multiobjective Pareto optimization, and model-free Q-learning for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Pretreatment CT data from 402 patients were used for model development and internal validation, with 110 patients forming a held-out external cohort. The final radiomics model achieved an external C-index of 0.707 (95% CI 0.627-0.783); high-risk patients had worse overall survival (HR 3.461, 95% CI 1.674-7.153), with minimal change after adjustment for histology (HR 3.444, 95% CI 1.662-7.137). Gene set enrichment and single-sample pathway analyses identified exploratory associations involving E2F targets, MYC targets V1, inflammatory response, and hypoxia, although no pathway met FDR < 0.05. LINCS L1000 perturbational profiles were evaluated using transcriptomic reversal, pathway specificity, and a feasibility-related proxy, with 4188 compounds retained in the common complete-case analysis. Multiobjective Pareto optimization was combined with three-split consensus ranking and sequential policy evaluation. TWS-119 showed consistent prioritization across all three splits (ranks 1, 3, and 4) and was Pareto-optimal in each split. In simulation-based evaluation, model-free Q-learning achieved higher terminal-goal attainment than myopic and static policies across all three splits, with improvements of approximately 6.2-13.3 percentage points over the myopic comparator. These findings support ParetoRx as an exploratory framework for biologically informed compound prioritization and computational sequential decision-making, while independent drug response and clinical validation remain necessary.

articles.title: Panognostics-Plus: An Integrated Multi-Task AI Framework for Automated Panoramic Radiograph Interpretation with Dental Charting and Structured Reporting-Development and Technical Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Dental charting from panoramic radiographs is essential for clinical assessment, yet remains time-consuming. This study presents Panognostics-Plus, an automated cloud-based AI framework for panoramic radiograph analysis integrating dental charting and structured radiological reporting. Panognostics-Plus was developed using a retrospective dataset of 1,595 panoramic radiographs and a YOLO-based architecture comprising modules for dental anatomy, dental treatment, and periapical diagnostics. Anatomical structures and dental treatments were analyzed using a two-stage pipeline, whereas periapical lesions were analyzed by detection-and-classification. YOLOv8m, YOLOv9m, YOLO11m, and YOLO26m were benchmarked. Detection was evaluated by precision, sensitivity, F1-score, AP, and mAP; segmentation by IoU and Dice; and processing time. Model differences were assessed using Friedman tests with Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc comparisons. YOLO26m achieved the highest overall performance. The largest mAP0@50:0.95 gains were observed for crowns (+ 21.3%), radicular cysts (+ 20.5%), root canal treatments (+ 17.3%), bridges (+ 14.3%), periodontal bone level (+ 14.3%), and periapical granulomas (+ 13.5%). Dental implants achieved precision, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.99, 0.98, and 0.98, respectively. Radicular cysts achieved precision, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.95, 0.93, and 0.94 versus 0.92, 0.90, and 0.91 for periapical granulomas. Significant differences were observed in 8 of 10 detection tasks and all segmentation tasks (all p < 0.001); periodontal bone level (p = 0.193) and dental fillings (p = 0.073) were nonsignificant. Dice coefficients reached 0.97 for dental anatomy and 0.96 for dental treatments. The workflow generated a segmentation overlay, dental chart, and structured radiological report in 15 ± 1.4 s per radiograph. Panognostics-Plus may improve panoramic radiograph analysis and clinical efficiency, although further validation is required.

articles.title: MDF-Net: A Decoupled Multimodal Fusion Network with Contrastive Learning for Reliable Brain Tumor Segmentation on Multi-sequence MRI.
articles.abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tumors from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is critical for clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and longitudinal disease monitoring. Multimodal MRI provides complementary information across sequences, yet this complementarity is entangled with substantial cross-modal redundancy. Prevailing coupled fusion schemes merge modalities into a single shared space, where discriminative tumor-specific cues and redundant shared content are blended indiscriminately, an effect further aggravated by cross-scale feature inconsistency and by the difficulty of delineating small enhancing lesions. To address these issues, we recast multimodal segmentation as a decoupled representation learning problem and propose a Multimodal Decoupled Fusion Network (MDF-Net) that explicitly disentangles the fused representation into complementary and non-redundant components. At its core, a Tri-Branch Decoupling (TBD) module separates the fused features into spatial, channel, and instance components, and a Feature Contrastive Learning (FCL) objective enforces their complementarity while suppressing inter-branch redundancy. To provide scale-aware and locally coherent features for decoupling, an Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module and a Local Window Self-Attention (LWSA) module jointly model multi-scale context and local dependencies, while a dedicated Small Lesion Refinement (SLR) module improves the delineation of small and ambiguous enhancing tumors through multi-scale detection and boundary-aware refinement. Extensive experiments on two publicly available benchmarks, BraTS 2023 and FeTS 2022, demonstrate that MDF-Net achieves competitive and well-balanced performance relative to recent state-of-the-art methods across tumor sub-regions and multiple evaluation metrics, with particularly accurate whole-tumor boundary delineation. Ablation studies and feature-space visualizations further confirm that explicit decoupling yields a more structured embedding space and that each component makes a complementary contribution to segmentation performance.

articles.title: Clinical Context-Dependent Value of bpMRI-Derived Imaging Representations for Prostate Cancer Risk Stratification.
articles.abstract: The objective was to evaluate the clinical context-dependent value of biparametric MRI (bpMRI)-derived imaging representations for prostate cancer (PCa) risk stratification, with emphasis on whether imaging features provide complementary information in patients within the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) gray zone. This dual-campus retrospective study included 536 patients with pathologically confirmed PCa who underwent pretreatment bpMRI. Patients were classified as low/intermediate and high-risk according to NCCN criteria. Patients from Campus 1 were randomly divided into training and internal test cohorts, and Campus 2 served as an independent test cohort. Radiomics, vision transformer, and contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) features were extracted from T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, and apparent diffusion coefficient maps. Clinical and combined clinical-imaging models were developed. Performance was assessed using ROC analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and SHAP interpretation, with predefined evaluation in the PSA gray zone. In the independent test cohort, the combined model achieved the highest overall discrimination, with an AUC of 0.921, followed closely by the clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.907). Among imaging-only models, the radiomics model showed the highest overall AUC (0.844). SHAP identified PSA as the dominant predictor, indicating clinically driven overall performance. In the PSA gray zone, clinical and combined model performance declined (AUCs, 0.381 and 0.600), whereas CLIP achieved the highest AUC (0.785) and favorable net benefit. The value of bpMRI-derived imaging representations for PCa risk stratification is context-dependent. CLIP-derived representations may provide complementary discrimination when PSA-based information is less informative, supporting context-aware evaluation of imaging AI models.

articles.title: Imaging Subphenotypes of Thoracic Involvement in IgG4-Related Disease: A Latent Class Analysis.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Thoracic manifestations of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are heterogeneous. We aimed to identify distinct imaging subphenotypes using latent class analysis (LCA) of chest computed tomography (CT) features and assess their associations with clinical characteristics, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively included patients with IgG4-RD and CT-confirmed thoracic involvement. Baseline chest CT findings were independently assessed by two thoracic radiologists. LCA of binary CT features was performed to identify imaging subphenotypes. Clinical and serologic characteristics, extrathoracic involvement, radiologic outcomes, and relapse-free survival were compared across subphenotypes. Cox regression analyses were used to identify factors independently associated with relapse. RESULTS: Among 231 patients, bronchovascular bundle thickening was the most frequent CT finding (56.7%). LCA identified five imaging subphenotypes: bronchovascular bundle-lymph node (BVB-LN, 38.5%), nodular (13.9%), interstitial (13.0%), mediastinal-pleural (18.6%), and mixed (16.0%). These subphenotypes differed in age, respiratory symptoms, extrathoracic involvement, and immunologic profiles. The interstitial subphenotype had the lowest radiologic improvement rate (41.7%) and highest progression rate (37.5%). The mixed (hazard ratio [HR], 3.821; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.336-10.923; P = 0.012) and BVB-LN (HR, 2.804; 95% CI, 1.062-7.399; P = 0.037) subphenotypes were independently associated with higher relapse risk, whereas combined glucocorticoid and immunosuppressant therapy was associated with lower relapse risk (HR, 0.405; 95% CI, 0.223-0.735; P = 0.003). CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort, LCA identified five thoracic imaging subphenotypes of IgG4-RD with specific clinical profiles, radiologic outcomes, and relapse risk. External validation is required before broader generalization or adoption as a standard classification framework.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Gadolinium-Free Virtual Contrast-Enhanced MRI for Predicting Immediate HIFU Ablation Outcomes in Uterine Fibroids.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate assessment of microvascular perfusion is essential for predicting high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids. Contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) is widely used for vascular evaluation; however, gadolinium-based agents pose safety concerns and may interfere with temperature monitoring. This study aimed to generate synthetic CE-T1WI (Syn-CE-T1WI) from T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) using deep learning for predicting immediate HIFU ablation outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mask-guided 3D conditional generative adversarial network (3D-cGAN) was developed using magnetic resonance imaging data from 300 patients (240 training, 60 testing). Syn-CE-T1WI was generated from T2WI. Image quality was assessed using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and mean absolute error (MAE). Three radiologists performed blinded evaluations of image authenticity and quality. A binary classification task was used to compare Syn-CE-T1WI and Real-CE-T1WI for predicting HIFU outcomes. RESULTS: In the test set, PSNR was 27.05 ± 2.21 dB, SSIM was 0.825 ± 0.12, and MAE was 0.023. Radiologists achieved a mean accuracy of 52.8% in distinguishing real from synthetic images (all P > 0.05). Overall, 88.9% of Syn-CE-T1WI were rated clinically acceptable. For outcome prediction, Syn-CE-T1WI achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.713-0.763, comparable to Real-CE-T1WI (0.725-0.775; all P > 0.05). Combining Syn-CE-T1WI with T2WI yielded AUCs of 0.775-0.800, numerically higher than T2WI alone (0.713-0.763), and similar to T2WI + Real-CE-T1WI (0.800-0.813; all P > 0.05). CONCLUSION: The mask-guided 3D-cGAN enabled the generation of high-fidelity, gadolinium-free Syn-CE-T1WI that may support noninvasive prediction of immediate HIFU ablation outcomes in uterine fibroids.

articles.title: Quantifying "Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus"-like Brain Morphometry patterns in an Alzheimer's Disease Cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is largely underdiagnosed. It is a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive decline, and cognitive improvement may occur even with comorbid Alzheimer's disease. However, iNPH-related imaging features can overlap with age-related and neurodegenerative atrophy, making differentiation difficult. Automated morphometric profiling of NPH-like patterns in biomarker-defined Alzheimer's disease cohorts has not been systematically explored. This pilot study aimed to quantify iNPH-like brain morphometry in an Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort using deep-learning-based morphometry and automated callosal angle measurement. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included N=30 amyloid-negative reference iNPH patients and N=1003 ADNI participants with structural T1-weighted MRI and CSF biomarkers. Age- and sex-adjusted volumetric z-scores were obtained using a deep-learning-based morphometry algorithm. We derived an iNPH morphometric profile using principal component analysis and Gaussian modeling of the reference iNPH cohort and applied it to the ADNI participants to compute individual iNPH similarity scores. We also automated callosal angle measurement for further clinical representation. We compared scores across cognitive stages and biological Alzheimer's disease groups and evaluated against expert Radscale review. RESULTS: iNPH-like morphometry increased with cognitive impairment, with mean differences of 0.03 between cognitively normal and mild cognitive impairment (p=0.06), 0.06 between mild cognitive impairment and dementia (p<0.001), and 0.09 between cognitively normal and dementia groups (p<0.001). Among cognitively impaired participants, scores were higher in biologically-defined Alzheimer's disease patients than biologically-defined non-Alzheimer's disease patients (mean difference=0.08, p<0.001). The iNPH similarity score correlated most strongly with ventricular enlargement features. Automated callosal angle measurements showed high agreement with expert ratings (Gwet's AC1 = 0.939) and angles below 90° occurred in 1.5% of ADNI participants. CONCLUSIONS: Automated normative morphometric profiling and callosal angle quantification identified heterogeneous iNPH-like structural patterns in the ADNI cohort.
