These tools provide a scalable approach for characterizing iNPH-like imaging features in dementia cohorts where identifying a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive impairment remains relevant. Further clinical validation remains necessary.

articles.title: Brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression: Desynchronization between salience network neuropsychological connectivity and heart rate variability.
articles.abstract: Somatic depression is a distinct subtype of major depressive disorder, with a poorer response to treatment, an elevated risk of suicidal behaviour, and a worse prognosis. Interoception, the sense of internal bodily signals, is related to somatic symptoms. However, the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms of body brain communication remain unclear. 293 depressed patients (145 with somatic symptoms and 148 without), and 160 healthy controls underwent magnetoencephalography during a resting state. Both the intra- and inter-network neural oscillation patterns of the salience network, were computed, alongside and heart rate variability (HRV) as a measure of autonomic function. Individuals with somatic depression exhibited lower HRV, accompanied by theta hyper-connectivity within the salience network. Although higher theta connectivity was linked to increased HRV in controls, this correlation was attenuated or even reversed in patients with somatic depression. Our findings identify a specific pattern of brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression, characterized by disrupted communication between salience network theta oscillations and autonomic cardiac regulation. This provides novel neuroimaging evidence for body-brain communication deficits in a clinically important depression subtype.

articles.title: Concurrent Prefrontal Neurochemical Effects of High-Definition Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation: Directional E-field Associations with GABA⁺ and Glx.
articles.abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) is a promising neuromodulatory technique for treating neuropsychiatric disorders. However, its neurochemical mechanisms remain poorly characterized, and clinical efficacy is limited by substantial inter-individual variability. This study used concurrent high-definition tDCS (HD-tDCS) and magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) to investigate neurochemical changes and their relationship with the induced electric field (E-field). In this randomized, sham-controlled, crossover study, 20 healthy adults were included in the final analysis. All participants underwent anodal HD-tDCS (2 mA, 10 min) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Concurrent MRS was performed at baseline, during, and post-stimulation. Individualized E-field simulations were performed using SimNIBS, extracting the E-field magnitude, normal, and tangential components within the MRS voxel. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess the effects of stimulation on metabolite changes, and Pearson correlations were performed to evaluate associations between neurochemical modulation and E-field metrics. Active anodal HD-tDCS induced significant post-stimulation reductions in both gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA⁺) (p = 0.047) and Glx (glutamate + glutamine) (p = 0.030) relative to sham. GABA⁺ decreases were negatively correlated with E-field magnitude (r = -0.479, p = 0.045) and the tangential component (r = -0.496, p = 0.037), whereas Glx reduction was associated with the normal E-field component (r = -0.529, p = 0.024). These findings indicate that prefrontal HD-tDCS induces concurrent neurochemical modulation with direction-specific E-field relationships, providing mechanistic insight into how E-field orientation may shape neurochemical responsiveness and supporting personalized neuromodulation.

articles.title: Temporal coupling shapes the effects of prolonged muscle-tendon vibration on sensorimotor EEG activity during motor imagery.
articles.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) recruits sensorimotor networks overlapping those engaged during physical execution and represents a promising rehabilitation tool. While concurrent afferent stimulation enhances MI-related cortical engagement, the effects of prolonged proprioceptive conditioning prior to MI remain unexplored. This study investigated whether prolonged muscle-tendon vibration (MTV) could modulate cortical activity during subsequent MI, indexed by electroencephalographic alpha- and beta-band event-related desynchronization (ERD). Twenty healthy adults performed imagined maximal isometric knee extensions before and after 20-minute suprapatellar MTV (100 Hz) or SHAM vibration (30 Hz with foam interface) in counterbalanced sessions. Cortical engagement was assessed via EEG burst detection over central electrodes (C3, Cz, C4). Maximal force capacity, submaximal force estimation performance, and cortical responses during combined MI and MTV were also evaluated. MTV induced stronger vibratory responses than SHAM, consistent with enhanced proprioceptive afferent activation. Following MTV, voluntary force outcomes showed near-threshold changes consistent with the expected direction, namely reduced maximal force capacity and altered submaximal force calibration, suggesting modified proprioceptive feedback. MI performed after MTV conditioning exhibited reduced alpha- and beta-band ERD compared to SHAM, with greater vibratory-induced responses being associated with a less pronounced post-vibration beta ERD. Conversely, when MI was performed concurrently with MTV following conditioning, alpha-band ERD increased selectively in the MTV session, with no modulation in the beta band. These findings suggest that prolonged proprioceptive conditioning modulates MI-related cortical engagement differently depending on the sensorimotor context in which imagery is performed. Such state-dependent effects may support distinct intervention strategies aimed either at recalibrating maladaptive sensorimotor patterns or at enhancing cortical recruitment in rehabilitation contexts.

articles.title: Repetition Dissociates Pointer and Content-based Representations in Visual Working Memory: Contrasting the CDA with Multivariate Shape Decoding.
articles.abstract: Memorizing a new phone number or address is hard at first, but becomes easier with repetition, as information shifts from working memory to long-term memory. Here we investigated how repetition affects the storage and transition of different aspects of mnemonic information by comparing univariate neural markers of active object storage with multivariate decoding of memory content. Thirty participants encoded lateralized stimuli from a continuous shape space into memory. Memory items were repeated six times in a row to induce learning. In line with earlier work, EEG recordings revealed that repetition led to a reduction in contralateral delay activity (CDA), a measure of active storage that has been taken to reflect a pointer-like representation of the individual object or its original source. In contrast, shape decoding during the retention and also after an impulse perturbation remained constant across repetitions. These results suggest that learning over repetitions reflects the abolishment of active and individuated object memory representations while passive, source-independent memory representations are retained.

articles.title: Impact of sexological follow-up on the sexual function of patients treated with chemo-radiotherapy and brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer: results of the prospective FEMINICOL study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Radiotherapy and brachytherapy (BT) for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) are associated with high rates of sexual morbidity, particularly vaginal stenosis. The prospective FEMINICOL study assessed sexual function and vaginal toxicity in patients treated with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and image-guided adaptive BT, with systematic sexological support. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre prospective cohort study (NCT03956498) included patients treated with concomitant CRT and BT between October 2019 and December 2020. A certified sex therapist met each patient before BT, at 2 months and 1 year after treatment. The primary objective was to evaluate sexual function one year after treatment using the FSFI questionnaire. RESULTS: Sixty patients were included in the study. Among patients who received clinical follow-up (54 at 2 months and 47 at 1 year), compliance with sexological follow-up was 98.1 % (53/54) at two months and 100 % at one year. Fifty-six patients with baseline evaluation and at least one post-treatment evaluation were analyzed. Median age was 54.5 years (31-77). At one year, 55.3 % of patients adhered to vaginal rehabilitation and 45.7 % were sexually active. Median FSFI score improved from 4 (range: 2-33.2) at baseline to 12.5 (2-34.8) at 1 year (paired test p < 0.001). Median sexual activity (QLQ-CX24) increased from 0 (0-66.7) to 33.3 (0-100) at 1 year (p < 0.001), while sexual anxiety remained stable (p = 0.93). At 1 year, Grade ≥ 3 vaginal toxicity occurred in 12.7 % of patients, mainly narrowing (8.5 %). Most patients (81.4 %) were satisfied with the sexological support. CONCLUSION: In this prospective cohort, systematic sexological support during and after CRT and BT was feasible and was associated with encouraging compliance with vaginal rehabilitation and favorable sexual function outcomes over time.

articles.title: Imaging-based strategies to optimize preoperative evaluation in invasive lobular Carcinoma: Impact of delayed-phase MRI and modified US thresholds for lymph nodes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether delayed-phase dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) improves MRI-histopathology size agreement and whether modifying the ultrasonographic cortical thickness threshold improves diagnosis of axillary lymph node metastasis in invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) compared with invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). METHODS: This retrospective study included 1,473 consecutive patients with 1,531 breast cancers (128 ILCs, 1,403 IDCs) who underwent preoperative ultrasonography, DCE-MRI, and surgery from March 2020 to December 2021. Tumor size was measured on early- and delayed-phase DCE-MRI. Differences in MRI-histopathologic size were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Spearman's correlation coefficient (ρ) values were compared using bootstrapping. Diagnostic performance of lymph node evaluation using current 2.5 mm and modified 2.0 mm and 3.0 mm thresholds was compared by McNemar's test. RESULTS: Tumor size on early-phase MRI was significantly underestimated in ILC than in IDC (mean discrepancy - 0.9 ± 2.2 cm vs. 0.1 ± 1.4 cm, p < 0.001). In ILC, MRI-histopathologic size correlation coefficient was greater on delayed-phase than on early-phase (ρ = 0.714 vs. 0.555; p < 0.001). In IDC, early-phase was more strongly correlated than delayed-phase (ρ = 0.760 vs. 0.726; p < 0.001). For ILC, modifying threshold did not improve diagnostic performance. Compared with the 2.5 mm threshold, at 2.0 mm, sensitivity (51.5 % [17/33] vs. 60.6 % [20/33], p = 0.25) were comparable and specificity decreased (90.5 % [86/95] vs. 75.8 % [72/95], p < 0.001); however, at 3.0 mm, sensitivity decreased (33.3 % [11/33], p = 0.03) and specificity (93.7 % [89/95], p = 0.25) were comparable. CONCLUSION: Delayed-phase DCE-MRI may improve tumor size estimation in ILC, while early-phase DCE-MRI remains suitable for IDC. Modifying cortical thickness threshold does not improve nodal diagnostic accuracy.

articles.title: Motion-guided semi-supervised learning with dynamic kernels for cardiac cine segmentation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Accurate segmentation of full cardiac cine magnetic resonance (CMR) sequences is crucial for clinical diagnosis. Although deep learning models have become the standard for this task, they typically require exhaustive frame-by-frame supervision, making manual data annotation prohibitively time-consuming. APPROACH: To address this, we propose a novel motion-guided semi-supervised spatiotemporal framework that propagates sparse supervision from the label of the end-diastolic (ED) frame to the entire sequence. Our framework jointly optimizes motion estimation and segmentation. First, a motion decoder estimates dense displacement fields to warp the ED label, generating high-fidelity pseudo-labels for unannotated frames. Concurrently, the segmentation network employs a Temporal Kernel Segmentation (TKS) module with dynamic convolutions to adaptively capture rapid cardiac deformations, alongside a Multi-Scale Spatial Propagator (MSP) to recover fine anatomical boundaries. The motion-derived pseudo-labels directly supervise the segmentation network, ensuring temporal coherence. MAIN RESULTS: Extensive experiments on a multi-center cohort from three clinical centers demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the compared methods, achieving superior segmentation accuracy and robust generalization capabilities. SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed framework effectively mitigates the burden of manual data annotation while providing temporally coherent full-cycle cardiac analysis, holding significant potential for efficient and reliable clinical assessment of cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Prostate: simplified MRI anatomy recognition and training-the P-SMART study: a novel approach to defining prostatic apex, mid-gland and base.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Precise lesion localisation on prostate MRI-specifically, identification of whether at the apex, mid-gland, or base-is essential for effective communication and clinical management. This study aimed to assess interobserver agreement of current practice using the Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) against a novel anatomy-based approach, P-SMART (Prostate Simplified MRI Anatomy Recognition and Training). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multi-reader, two-phase agreement study, used axial and sagittal T2-weighted MRI from a publicly available dataset. Forty MRI cases were annotated with four regions of interest (ROIs). Readers were asked to document ROI location-apex, mid-gland, or base-first using the PI-RADS method, then following a 3-week washout period and short educational intervention, using the P-SMART method. Interobserver agreement was evaluated using Fleiss' kappa (κ) statistics and compared following bootstrap resampling using a paired t-test. Subgroup analyses were performed by reader expertise and prostate size. RESULTS: Following quality assurance, 156 ROIs were evaluated by 43 readers in each phase of the study. Overall interobserver agreement improved with P-SMART vs PI-RADS (κ = 0.571 vs 0.399; p < 0.001). In subgroup analyses, improvements were consistent for experts (0.663 vs 0.435; p < 0.001), non-experts (0.530 vs 0.393; p < 0.001), large prostates (0.518 vs 0.325; p < 0.001), and small prostates (0.620 vs 0.461; p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The P-SMART approach, designed to align with the PI-RADS sector map, yielded significantly higher interobserver agreement for prostate lesion-level localisation than the PI-RADS method, across reader experience and gland size, though overall agreement was only moderate. Improved reproducibility may support biopsy targeting, active surveillance monitoring, and treatment planning. KEY POINTS: Question Can a novel method of dividing the prostate into apex, mid-gland, and base improve reader agreement compared to current practice? Findings The P-SMART method to divide the prostate outperformed PI-RADS (Fleiss' kappa 0.571 vs 0.399), improving consistency across experience levels and prostate sizes. RELEVANCE STATEMENT: More reproducible prostate level assignment supports accurate lesion localisation for biopsy planning, active surveillance, and treatment planning. If validated, P-SMART may improve communication and could be integrated into reporting workflows and software tools.

articles.title: Application of topological deep learning in staging liver fibrosis based on hepatobiliary phase MR images.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early-stage liver fibrosis is reversible; thus, accurate staging of liver fibrosis is of great importance.. Liver biopsy is the gold standard for the diagnosis of liver fibrosis; however, its invasive nature limits its clinical application. Accurate noninvasive staging of liver fibrosis remains challenging. Thus, there is an urgent need for a precise and reliable noninvasive diagnostic approach. OBJECTIVES: A topological deep learning model combining topological data analysis and EfficientViT framework (TopoEfficientViT) was developed to effectively capture global contextual relationships in hepatobiliary phase MR images for assessment of staging liver fibrosis. METHODS: Our retrospective study included patients with chronic liver diseases from June 2018 to July 2025, which was approved by our Institutional Review Board. Our data from a hospital site (Site A) in our institution were divided into a training set (n = 275) and a validation set (n = 75). The test set (n=65) was composed of data from a separate hospital site (Site B) in the same institution. RESULTS: A total of 415 patients (323 males, mean age 56.52±9.54 years; 92 females, mean age 58.86±9.68 years) were enrolled in the study. In the training set, the AUC and accuracy of TopoEfficientViT for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.942 and 0.906, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.957 and 0.891, respectively. In the validation set, the AUC and accuracy for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.849 and 0.76, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.861and 0.813, respectively. In the test set, the AUC and accuracy for staging liver fibrosis F1-2 vs. F3-4 were 0.829 and 0.769, respectively; for staging liver fibrosis F1-3 vs. F4 were 0.791 and 0.785, respectively. CONCLUSION: The TopoEfficientViT model had high predictive performance for staging liver fibrosis by integrating multi-scale persistent homology topology with convolutional networks.

articles.title: Deep learning-based detection and classification of airway nodules on CT for early medical intervention.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Airway lesions are common CT findings in interval and post-screen lung cancers; however, airway nodules are frequently overlooked. Robust artificial intelligence (AI) tools for characterizing airway nodules remain limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning-based models for the detection and classification of airway nodules on low-dose CT(LDCT) as a second-reading tool. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 1813 segmental and more proximal airway nodules were retrospectively identified from 1107 LDCT of 1043 participants. A sphere-based center-points matching network, first used to establish a lung nodule detection model, was transferred to airway nodules and enhanced by incorporating coordinate and multiscale attention. The model was trained on 907 proximal airway nodules and independently tested on 738 proximal nodules across four hospitals. The clinical utility of the AI tool was evaluated through human-AI interaction. For nodule classification, a 3D SEResNeXt101-based model was trained, validated and tested using 286 airway nodules (121 benign, 165 malignant) with a 6:2:2 split and evaluated in an independent testing dataset. RESULTS: On the independent testing set, the detection model achieved a high sensitivity of 73.7%. Human-AI interaction demonstrated AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' performance, increasing sensitivity from 39.5% to 72.9% and F1-score from 49.4% to 77.2%, while reducing diagnosis time from 83.8 s to 61.8 s. The classification model showed high sensitivities of 82.1%, 71.4%, 94.3%, 72.7% and specificities of 62.7%, 73.9%, 73.9%, 87.5% across multicenter training, validation, testing and independent testing sets, respectively. CONCLUSION: This AI system significantly enhances the detection and classification of proximal airway nodules, guiding early medical intervention. KEY POINTS: Question Improved early detection and classification of airway nodules are critical for lung cancer mortality reduction, but AI-based CAD systems targeting airway nodules remain scarce. Findings The DL models for detection and classification of proximal airway nodules on chest CT were developed and assisted radiologists to achieve higher detection accuracy. Critical Relevance Statement The clinical applications of the proposed DL-based system for detecting and classifying proximal airway nodules on chest CT scans help radiologists reduce missed/delayed diagnoses and shorten diagnostic time as a second-reading tool, guiding medical intervention and improving clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Safety profile of a location-tailored short DAPT protocol for intracranial aneurysms treated with flow diversion.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: There is no consensus on antiplatelet management after flow-diverter (FD) deployment. While prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remains common, this approach carries haemorrhagic risks. We evaluated the safety of a short, location-tailored DAPT protocol for patients treated with FDs for intracranial aneurysms. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients undergoing elective FD treatment for intracranial aneurysms in our department. Patients followed a post-procedural DAPT protocol tailored to target vessel location: 1-month DAPT for internal carotid (ICA) and vertebral arteries (VA), and 3-month for other locations, followed by single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT). Periprocedural and delayed thromboembolic and haemorrhagic complications were assessed. RESULTS: Seventy-five patients with 82 aneurysms were included. Median DAPT duration was 43.0 days (IQR: 34.0-92.0) for ICA/VA, and 93.5 days (IQR: 90.7-99.0) for other locations. Periprocedural symptomatic neurological thromboembolic complications occurred in 1/82 (1.2%) of procedures, while no periprocedural neurological haemorrhagic complications occurred. Delayed symptomatic neurological thromboembolic complications occurred in 1/75 patients (1.3%) during DAPT, 2/75 (2.7%) after DAPT discontinuation, 1/55 (1.8%) after SAPT discontinuation. Delayed neurological haemorrhagic complications were 0%; other delayed haemorrhagic complications occurred in 2/75 patients (2.7%) during DAPT and 1/75 (1.3%) during SAPT. Adequate aneurysm occlusion was achieved in 72.9% of cases at angiographic follow-up (median 205.5 days, IQR: 183.8-239.0). At the last clinical follow-up (median 707.0 days, IQR: 389.5-998.5), overall mortality was 0% and permanent morbidity was 2.7%. CONCLUSIONS: A short vessel-tailored DAPT protocol is a safe and feasible management strategy for intracranial FD treatments, demonstrating low thromboembolic and haemorrhagic risks.

articles.title: CT-based bone mineral density estimation using HU, radiomics, and deep learning.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and test models that estimate bone mineral density (BMD) from thoracolumbar junction CT images using Hounsfield unit (HU) assessment, radiomics, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients who underwent lumbar dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry and CT covering T12 and L1 within 6 months at four hospitals between 2014 and 2025. In total, 465 patients were eligible for T12 analysis, and 448 for L1. Data from two institutions were used for training/validation and data from the other two for external testing. We developed five models: region-of-interest-based HU regression; volume-of-interest (VOI)-based HU regression; radiomics; CNN; and an ensemble combining VOI, radiomics, and CNN. Performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R2), and Bland-Altman limits of agreement (LoA). RESULTS: For T12, the CNN model performed best among the single models (MAE: 0.122, RMSE: 0.157, R2: 0.603), whereas the ensemble model showed a slightly higher MAE (0.128) but lower RMSE (0.154) and higher R2 (0.620). For L1, the radiomics model was the best single model (MAE: 0.124, RMSE: 0.155, R2: 0.582), while the ensemble showed numerically improved performance (MAE: 0.116, RMSE: 0.145, R2: 0.633). Pairwise comparisons showed no significant difference in absolute prediction errors between the ensemble and the best single model at either T12 or L1. CONCLUSION: We developed an ensemble framework integrating volumetric HU assessment, radiomics, and CNNs to estimate BMD from thoracolumbar junction CT images. External testing across two independent institutions demonstrated promising performance for BMD estimation.

articles.title: Comparison of braided versus laser-cut stent placement for ruptured intracranial aneurysms in the acute phase: a propensity score matched study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare clinical and angiographic outcomes between braided and laser-cut stents in patients with acutely ruptured intracranial aneurysms undergoing stent-assisted coiling (SAC), using propensity score matching (PSM) to adjust for confounders. METHODS: This study analyzed consecutive patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage who underwent SAC within 72 h of onset between January 2017 and June 2024 from a prospectively maintained registry. Clinical and angiographic outcomes were compared before and after 1:1 PSM. Subgroup analyses explored effect modifiers. RESULTS: A total of 552 patients were enrolled (384 laser-cut and 168 braided), with a mean age of 60.32 years and 64.3% females. In the matched cohort (161 pairs), perioperative complications, and aneurysm occlusion and functional outcomes did not differ significantly (all P > 0.05) at 6-month follow-up. In the entire cohort, laser-cut stents were associated with lower odds of favorable functional prognosis at discharge than braided stents (OR = 0.53, 95% CI 0.31-0.89). Significant interactions were observed between stent type and hypertension (P for interaction = 0.009) and irregular aneurysm morphology (P for interaction = 0.010) for incomplete occlusion. CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference in safety or efficacy was observed between braided and laser-cut stents in acutely ruptured intracranial aneurysms. The interactions with hypertension and irregular morphology warrant attention when individualizing stent selection and planning follow-up angiography. Larger multicenter, adequately powered prospective studies with standardized antithrombotic regimens are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Characterization of local linearity in deep learning CT denoising networks.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep learning algorithms for image processing have been proposed for a wide range of applications. In particular, deep learning CT denoising has demonstrated superior ability to reduce noise compared to conventional methods. However, the nonlinear nature of these algorithms makes it difficult to inspect and visualize how the model accomplishes the denoising task. PURPOSE: We propose a local linearization approach to characterize and analyze the behavior of deep learning algorithms. Example analysis was performed for a classic denoising architecture with convolutional neural network and ReLU activation functions, and was extended to GELU activation and a transformer-based architecture. METHODS: We defined strictly local linear regions as the input space over which the activation patterns of all ReLU activation functions are the same. The extent of these regions was investigated by perturbing clinically relevant features of a lung lesion. We further defined approximately local linear regions as the input space where Jacobians are similar and linear approximation results in small error. We developed an algorithm to partition input space over a range of lesion and background features into approximately local linear regions, and separately quantified the contribution of the noise realization and anatomical background to this approximation error. The behavior of networks trained with different levels of denoising, as well as alternative architectures, was compared. RESULTS: The extent of strictly local linear regions was found to be very small. Perturbations on the scale of  10 - 8  mm - 1    were enough to push the network to a neighboring strictly local linear region. However, the Jacobians over a large number of strictly local linear regions were found to be highly similar, which suggests that the network behaves approximately as a piecewise linear system. The partitioning algorithm identified a small number of approximately local linear regions within input spaces characterized by clinically relevant features; this number was similar for the GELU variant but increased for networks trained with more aggressive noise reduction and for a transformer-based architecture, while Jacobians transferred across anatomical backgrounds also increased approximation error. CONCLUSIONS: The local linearity analysis framework can be a useful tool for elucidating the behavior of neural networks that are traditionally considered as "black-boxes." Preliminary results suggest that the framework can be applied to other differentiable architectures, subject to empirical validation, to characterize these highly nonlinear, data-dependent algorithms over input spaces of interest.

articles.title: Double-bowtie filter design for pediatric spectral CT imaging: A fan beam simulation study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite concerns about radiation dose in pediatric patients, computed tomography (CT) remains a first-line imaging modality for children. Spectral CT provides additional diagnostic information that benefits pediatric imaging. However, most existing spectral CT systems are primarily optimized for adult patients. PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate a novel double bowtie filter integrating a K-edge material layer with a conventional Teflon filter for CT. The proposed design aims to enhance spectral signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and spectral separation within the projection domain while maintaining radiation dose levels suitable for pediatric imaging. METHODS: A simulation framework was developed and used to model a rapid kVp-switching CT system operating at 70/110 kVp with realistic tube power and geometric constraints. Pediatric phantoms of three sizes (100-200 mm anterior-posterior width) were used to evaluate performance. Five accessible and safe filter materials-gadolinium (Gd), holmium (Ho), erbium (Er), silver (Ag), and tin (Sn)-were tested in combination with a Teflon bowtie. System performance was quantified using virtual monoenergetic image (VMI) SNR at 40 and 70 keV, and the area under the monoenergetic SNR curve (AUMC) as a comprehensive spectral image quality metric. Dose consistency was ensured using a traditional Teflon bowtie as the reference. RESULTS: The Teflon + Gd configuration achieved the highest performance, improving mean AUMC over all fan angles by 53.6% on average and up to 56% for the largest phantom. VMI SNR increased by approximately 46% at 40 keV and 42% at 70 keV. CONCLUSIONS: The double-bowtie concept substantially enhances spectral performance. The Teflon + Gd design provides a manufacturable, pediatric-optimized solution adaptable to kVp-switching and other spectral CT architectures, offering improved diagnostic quality at low dose levels.

articles.title: Longitudinal Cardiac MRI Reveals Phenotypic Evolution of MYBPC3-Associated Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Following Acute Myocarditis.
Ultrasound Pattern-Based Malignancy Risk Stratification and Subcategorization of K-TIRADS Intermediate-Suspicion Thyroid Nodules to Improve Biopsy Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an ultrasound (US) pattern-based subcategorization system for Korean Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (K-TIRADS) 4 nodules and to compare it with US feature-based subcategorization system and 2021 K-TIRADS as biopsy criteria. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Overall, 1,409 K-TIRADS 4 nodules (>1 cm) with final diagnoses, including 190 malignant lesions, were included. A US pattern-based subcategorization system for K-TIRADS 4 nodules was developed using US predictors of malignancy in each of the following three subgroups defined according to the 2021 K-TIRADS: solid hypoechoic nodules without suspicious features (subgroup 1), partially cystic or iso-/hyperechoic nodules with suspicious features (subgroup 2), and diffuse infiltrative lesions (subgroup 3). The biopsy criterion modified according to US pattern-based subcategorization (>1 cm for K-TIRADS 4B and >1.5 cm for K-TIRADS 4A) was compared with those based on the US feature-based subcategorization system and the 2021 K-TIRADS in terms of theoretical sensitivity (cancers detected at biopsy/all cancers), diagnostic yield (cancers detected at biopsy/all nodules), and unnecessary biopsy rate (benign lesions undergoing biopsy/all nodules). RESULTS: The US pattern-based subcategorization criteria included macrocalcification in subgroup 1, rim calcification or at least two suspicious features in subgroup 2, and a diffuse infiltrative pattern in subgroup 3; these criteria significantly increased malignancy risk (P < 0.001). Nodules were subcategorized as K-TIRADS 4B (higher malignancy risk, 38.6%) or K-TIRADS 4A (lower malignancy risk, 9.3%; P < 0.001). Compared with the >1.5-cm criterion and the US feature-based criterion, the modified biopsy criterion based on US pattern-based subcategorization significantly increased sensitivity by 17.4 percentage points (%p) and 10.0%p, diagnostic yield by 2.3%p and 1.3%p, and the unnecessary biopsy rate by 4.4%p and 2.9%p, respectively (all P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: As a biopsy criterion, US pattern-based subcategorization significantly improved sensitivity and diagnostic yield, with only small increases in the unnecessary biopsy rate compared with the other two criteria. US pattern-based subcategorization may provide an intuitive and clinically effective method for risk stratification and management of K-TIRADS 4 thyroid nodules.

articles.title: Enhancing Radiologists' Diagnostic Performance for Primary Bone Tumors Using Structured Report-Driven Assistance From Multiple Large Language Models.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine whether artificial intelligence (AI) assistance through structured report-driven diagnostic suggestions ensembled from multiple large language models (LLMs) can improve radiologists' diagnostic accuracy for primary bone tumors. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively included the data of 232 patients (15 for prompt development and 217 for testing) with pathologically confirmed primary bone tumors (January 2019-January 2026) who underwent MRI and either radiography or CT. Three radiologists with different levels of expertise generated structured radiology reports and established diagnoses with and without LLM assistance. The structured radiology reports were input into an output-ensemble pipeline of four LLMs (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6, and Llama 4 Maverick), generating ranked differential diagnoses aggregated across models and model-specific justifications, which radiologists reviewed to establish LLM-assisted diagnoses. Generalized linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate the LLM-assistance effect on the Top-1 and Top-3 diagnostic accuracies. The readers' responses to correct and incorrect multi-LLM diagnostic suggestions (acceptance or rejection) were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: Across the three readers, LLM assistance significantly improved the overall Top-1 and Top-3 accuracies from 57.1% to 72.0% and from 81.1% to 90.9%, respectively (both adjusted P < 0.001). Top-1 accuracy increased by 6.5, 14.3, and 24.0 percentage points for the most- to least-experienced readers, respectively, while Top-3 accuracy increased by 4.2, 7.4, and 18.0 percentage points, respectively. Reader responses to multi-LLM suggestions differed by experience: less-experienced readers accepted incorrect suggestions more frequently, whereas the most-experienced reader rejected incorrect suggestions more frequently but also rejected correct suggestions more often. The multi-LLM ensemble showed a standalone Top-1 accuracy ranging from 56.7% to 62.2% and Top-3 accuracy ranging from 85.3% to 86.6%. CONCLUSION: Structured report-driven multi-LLM assistance improves radiologists' performance for diagnosing primary bone tumors. The readers' responses to AI suggestions varied according to their experience levels. Although numerically greater increments in the diagnostic accuracy were observed with decreasing reader experience, this observation requires further validation using larger reader samples.

articles.title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR. RESULTS: Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia. CONCLUSION: Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

articles.title: Multiphasic CT radiomics-clinical model for predicting acute pancreatitis recurrence: a multicenter survival analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating multiphasic CT radiomics and clinical variables to estimate recurrence risk after first-episode acute pancreatitis (AP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 548 patients with first-episode AP (training, n = 272; internal validation, n = 117; external validation, n = 159). Clinical and multiphasic CT data were collected, with recurrence as the primary endpoint. After stability-based feature selection, clinical, radiomics, and combined Cox models were constructed. Performance was evaluated using the C-index and time-dependent AUC, with SHAP for interpretability. RESULTS: A total of 548 patients were included (median age 42 years; 363 men). Recurrence rates were similar across cohorts (30.1%, 29.9%, and 28.3%; p = 0.702). The combined model achieved C-indices of 0.783 and 0.775 in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, numerically higher than those of the clinical model (0.748 and 0.750) and radiomics model (0.647 and 0.619), although the incremental improvement over the clinical model was not statistically significant. In the external validation cohort, time-dependent AUCs remained acceptable through 36 months but declined at 48 months. High-risk patients had lower 3-year recurrence-free survival than low-risk patients (37.4% vs 86.8%; log-rank p < 0.001). SHAP analysis identified the NC-3mm-Radscore as the most influential imaging-derived variable, whereas etiology-targeted prevention was the dominant protective factor. CONCLUSIONS: The combined model demonstrated acceptable discrimination for predicting recurrence within the first 24 months after first-episode AP and may facilitate individualized follow-up and secondary prevention strategies. KEY POINTS: Question Can a multiphasic CT radiomics-clinical model improve prediction of AP recurrence over clinical factors alone in a multicenter setting? Findings The combined model demonstrated numerically higher predictive performance than the clinical model, though the incremental improvement was not statistically significant. Critical relevance statement This study critically evaluates the added value of multiphasic radiomics for recurrence prediction in AP, demonstrating that while radiomics captures baseline microenvironmental vulnerability, post-discharge clinical interventions remain the dominant dynamic drivers.

articles.title: Synthetic CT from biplanar radiographs for patellofemoral anatomical assessment: development and validation of an adapted X2CT-GAN model.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Accurate assessment of osseous morphology is essential for the diagnosis and surgical management of patellofemoral instability. Methods capable of providing CT-like anatomical information while reducing radiation exposure are therefore of considerable clinical interest. This study aimed to validate the accuracy of radiography-derived synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated by a deep learning model for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability. METHODS: A total of 210 paired radiographs and CT scans were retrospectively collected and randomly divided into a training set (n = 170) and a validation set (n = 40). A deep learning model based on the X2CT-GAN framework was used to reconstruct sCT volumes from anteroposterior and lateral radiographs. Two blinded readers independently measured tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance, trochlear sulcus angle, and Caton-Deschamps index on both sCT and real CT images. Reliability, inter-modality agreement, and threshold-based classification agreement were evaluated. RESULTS: All intra- and inter-observer reliability values were excellent. Inter-modality agreement was excellent for TT-TG distance and good for trochlear sulcus angle. Agreement for patellar height was good. The mean absolute error for TT-TG distance ranged from 1.24 to 1.38 mm. Agreement for threshold-based classifications ranged from substantial to almost perfect, with high specificity observed across all evaluated cutoff values. CONCLUSIONS: Radiography-derived sCT demonstrated good agreement with real CT for both quantitative measurements and threshold-based classifications relevant to clinical decision-making in patellofemoral instability. These findings suggest that radiography-derived synthetic CT may represent a promising lower-radiation alternative for anatomical assessment of patellofemoral instability in selected clinical scenarios.

articles.title: Relationships between cam morphology and [18F]sodium fluoride PET uptake in asymptomatic hips.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Bone deformities are linked to femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) and increased risk of hip osteoarthritis (OA) but are also common in the general population. The purpose of this study is to examine relationships between FAI-linked morphology and resting bone metabolic activity in asymptomatic hips. METHODS: This exploratory secondary analysis of hip scans from a [18F]NaF PET-MRI study on knee pain included 76 asymptomatic hips from 41 individuals (53 ± 13 years, body mass index 25.9 ± 5.1 kg/m2, 21 female/20 male). Hips were evaluated for cam, pincer, and additional morphology with the Hip Osteoarthritis MRI Scoring System. Mean and maximum PET standardized uptake values (SUV) were recorded for the femoral head-neck junction, center of the femoral head, and anterolateral acetabulum. The influence of morphology on SUVmean and SUVmax was assessed with linear mixed effects models. RESULTS: Forty-two hips had isolated cam morphology, two had isolated pincer morphology, and four had mixed-type morphology. Cam morphology or alpha angles were not associated with increased bone metabolic activity. Hips with gluteal tendinitis/trochanteric bursitis had significantly higher SUVmax in the center of the femoral head (p = 9.98e-5). No other morphological features were associated with bone metabolic activity, though the low prevalence of features such as pincer morphology limits interpretation of these findings. CONCLUSION: In older asymptomatic hips without OA, no association was detected between cam morphology and elevated resting bone remodeling. Understanding structure-function relationships in asymptomatic hips with cam morphology may help contextualize findings associated with pain in patients with FAI or OA.

articles.title: Enhancing the Motion Robustness of Breath-Held 3D T1-Weighted Abdominal MRI Using a Cartesian Acquisition With Spiral Profile Ordering.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate a novel self-gated motion-robust 3D T1-weighted gradient echo imaging framework based on a Cartesian acquisition with spiral profile ordering (CASPR) for abdominal imaging under unstable breath-hold conditions. METHODS: The CASPR trajectory was evaluated using frequency encoding in the anterior-to-posterior (AP) direction for respiratory motion robustness. The CASPR's intrinsic k-space center oversampling was exploited to directly extract a self-gated respiratory signal from the acquired data. A soft-gating motion compensation framework was integrated into the reconstruction pipeline. The method was validated in 10 healthy volunteers (five males and five females) and compared to a Cartesian acquisition with pseudorandom undersampling. RESULTS: Both CASPR and Cartesian acquisition with pseudorandom undersampling exhibited motion artifacts under unstable breath-hold conditions without retrospective correction. The proposed self-gated CASPR framework enabled reliable extraction of the respiratory signal directly from the AP readout. Soft gating significantly improved the image quality of motion-corrupted scans. CONCLUSION: This study introduces a novel self-gated CASPR-based framework for respiratory motion compensation in 3D abdominal MRI, in cases of incomplete and delayed breath-holds. The method enables the extraction of the self-navigator signal along the anterior-to-posterior axis and compensates for motion using a soft-gating technique.

articles.title: 2D U-Net Framework for Multiclass Automated Segmentation of Healthy Structures, Ischemic Stroke, and Glioblastoma in the Rat Brain.
articles.abstract: Rodents are essential for preclinical brain disease research, including stroke, tumors, and neurodegenerative disorders. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables longitudinal brain tissue visualization, but accurate segmentation is crucial for meaningful analysis. This study introduces a multitask 2D U-Net, a convolutional neural network designed for automated segmentation and quantification of brain regions, ischemic stroke lesions, and tumors in rats using T2-weighted imaging (T2-wi) and T2-relaxation maps. The model was evaluated on the following three MRI datasets: (i) segmentation of multiple brain regions in healthy rats, (ii) ischemic stroke lesions using T2-relaxation maps, and (iii) glioblastoma tumors using T2-wi. Performance was assessed using the Dice coefficient (DC), Hausdorff distance (HD), sensitivity (SEN), and volume ratio (VR), comparing network outputs against semiautomatic ground truths and existing models. A total of 1949 images from 111 rats were analyzed, expanded to 5847 through data augmentation. After correcting an animal-level train/test partitioning that prevented data leakage between subjects, the model achieved robust accuracy across all tasks (DC = 0.80-0.96, HD = 0.83-2.16 mm, SEN = 0.75-0.96, VR = 0.89-1.10), showing a strong correlation ( ρ = 0.82 - 0.99  ) with manual annotations. This framework improves segmentation accuracy, robustness, and applicability across different MRI settings and conditions, addressing issues like interrater variability and time inefficiency when analyzing rodent brain MRI data. Datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/NOBEL-MRI/Rat-Datasets.

articles.title: Scanner acoustic noise in resting-state fMRI.
articles.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) is usually acquired during rapid gradient switching that produces intense, spectrally structured sound. Scanner sound activates auditory pathways and can alter neural, vigilance, autonomic, respiratory, and movement-related states, but its sound-specific causal effect on intrinsic functional-connectivity estimates remains unresolved. Direct human comparisons are few and heterogeneous: some report stronger or more extensive network estimates under quieter acquisition, whereas others find broadly preserved topology and within-network connectivity. Near-silent Looping Star imaging can recover canonical resting-state networks with marked sound reduction, but reduced temporal signal-to-noise ratio and functional sensitivity expose a trade-off between acoustic burden and measurement performance. Most quiet-versus-standard contrasts simultaneously alter temporal sampling, gradient vibration, reconstruction, steady-state behavior, or image quality and therefore identify a total protocol effect rather than a sound-specific effect. A structured, original-scale comparison reports acoustic levels and metrics, measurement conditions, acquisition parameters, and resting-state outcomes without pooling unlike measures. Vigilance, autonomic activity, respiration, and movement are potential mediators; indiscriminate regression of these variables can remove part of the total acoustic effect. Current evidence establishes that acquisition protocols can alter rs-fMRI estimates and that scanner sound is biologically active, but it does not establish a universal, directionally uniform suppression of human resting-state connectivity by conventional echo-planar imaging. Future sound-specific attribution would require randomized within-subject manipulation, protected-ear frequency-resolved dosimetry, control of co-varying vibration and sequence properties, and synchronized state and physiological monitoring.

articles.title: Prenatal Ultrasound in Predicting the Need for Postnatal Surgery in Fetal Non-duodenal Small Bowel Dilation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The accuracy of prenatal ultrasound in recognizing fetal non-duodenal small bowel dilation (ND-SBD) due to obstructive conditions requiring neonatal surgery is not well established. We assessed the positive predictive value (PPV) of prenatal 2-dimensional (2D) ultrasound measurement of the small bowel diameter for identifying fetuses with ND-SBD who will require postnatal surgical intervention. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane with terms related to fetal bowel dilation and postnatal outcome. For each included study, we estimated the PPV of prenatal ultrasound in predicting the need for neonatal surgery among live-born, evaluable newborns classified as having a prenatal diagnosis of ND-SBD, and performed a Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of proportions to estimate the pooled PPV across studies. We identified 10 manuscripts, comprising 390 fetuses with a prenatal diagnosis of ND-SBD, of which 341 from 9 studies had data available for analysis. The observed PPV for postnatal surgery ranged from 8 to 82%, with a pooled estimate of 56% (90% credible interval (CrI) [44%, 67%]). Heterogeneity between studies was elevated, with an I2 of 84.8% (90% CrI [68.3%, 92.4%]) and a wide 90% posterior predictive interval of 19-89%, indicating substantial variability in the PPV across populations. Most studies presented high or unclear risk of bias and applicability concerns based on QUADAS-2 evaluation. 2D prenatal ultrasound evaluation of the fetal small intestine diameter has a moderate ability in predicting the need for postnatal surgery due to ND-SBD conditions. The substantial between-study heterogeneity and wide posterior predictive interval indicate considerable variation in the predictive value across populations and clinical settings, limiting the interpretation of the pooled PPV alone. Our findings highlight the need for prospective studies to better define the normal development of the fetal small intestine and identify prenatal ultrasound markers predicting non-duodenal small bowel abnormalities.

articles.title: An international women in radiology retreat: Design, impact, and a framework for leadership, community, and well-being.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Burnout among radiologists remains a global challenge and disproportionately affects women because of persistent inequities in leadership opportunities, mentorship, work-life integration, and professional advancement. While wellness initiatives have expanded, few interventions foster enduring professional relationships and community for women radiologists. This study describes the design and evaluation of an international retreat developed to promote leadership, collaboration, and physician well-being among women in radiology. METHODS: The American Association of Women in Radiology (AAWR) International Women in Radiology Retreat was designed to address challenges specific to women in radiology through a small-group, immersive experience emphasizing mentorship, reflective discussion, leadership development, and authentic connection rather than traditional didactic programming. Twenty-six women radiologists representing multiple countries and career stages participated. A post-retreat anonymous survey assessed participant experience through quantitative questions and qualitative free-text responses, analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Eighteen participants completed the survey (69% response rate). All respondents expressed interest in participating in future retreats. Qualitative analysis identified seven domains of impact: connection and community, shared experiences across cultures, professional growth, personal renewal, inspiration, networking and collaboration, and commitment to action. Participants also reported sustained engagement following the retreat through mentorship, communication, collaborative scholarship, and networking, suggesting benefits extending beyond the retreat. CONCLUSION: An intentionally designed, community-centered retreat may provide a reproducible framework for fostering leadership, professional fulfillment, and physician well-being among women radiologists. Incorporating principles of connection, mentorship, reflection, and belonging into retreats may represent an important strategy for addressing burnout, strengthening retention, and supporting a more sustainable radiology workforce.

articles.title: Time-dependent prediction of overt hepatic encephalopathy risk after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in cirrhosis.
articles.abstract: AIM: The aim of this study was to develop and externally validate a time-dependent model for predicting overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement in patients with cirrhosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-centre study included patients with cirrhosis who underwent TIPS between November 2018 and October 2024. Patients were assigned to training and external validation cohorts according to treatment centre. The primary outcome was post-TIPS OHE. Associations of demographic, laboratory, imaging and procedural variables with OHE were evaluated using Cox regression. The model was developed and validated internally and externally. Performance was assessed using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: A total of 561 patients were included, comprising 437 (77.9%) in the training and 124 (22.1%) in the external validation cohort. During a median follow-up of 25.0 months (interquartile range, 11.0-43.5), 108 patients (19.3%) developed OHE. Age, history of OHE, Child-Pugh class, and albumin and cholinesterase levels were retained in the final model. The model showed good discrimination, with a C-index of 0.762 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.710-0.814) in the training cohort and 0.801 (95% CI: 0.722-0.880) in the external validation cohort. Time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values were favourable across follow-up intervals. Calibration performance was acceptable, and DCA suggested potential clinical benefit. CONCLUSION: This time-dependent model may assist in post-TIPS OHE risk stratification and follow-up planning after haemodynamically successful shunt creation. However, prospective validation and comparison with established prediction tools are warranted before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Percutaneous tandem modified plastic stenting for post-transplant duct-to-duct biliary anastomotic strictures: long-term outcomes from a single-center cohort.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and long-term outcomes of a percutaneous technique using tandem modified plastic biliary stents (MPBSs) for benign duct-to-duct biliary anastomotic strictures after liver transplantation (LT). METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 48 recipients who underwent treatment between January 2011 and January 2025 after failure or ineligibility for endoscopic therapy. All patients underwent percutaneous placement of two MPBSs through a single transhepatic access. Technical success, symptomatic and biochemical response, procedure-related complications classified according to the Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe system, and patency were evaluated. Patency was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and laboratory parameters were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. RESULTS: Patients' mean age was 33.3 ± 22.0 years. Technical success was achieved in all patients (100%), and symptomatic and biochemical improvement was documented in 46 of 48 patients (95.8%); assessment timing was not standardized. The mean stent indwelling time was 159 ± 42.9 days. Stent migration occurred in 3 patients (6.2%), and cholangitis in 5 patients (10.4%), with no major complications observed. The median primary patency was 1,689 days (95% confidence interval: 311-3,067 days). During follow-up, 29 of 48 patients (60.4%) required at least one additional biliary intervention. Total bilirubin levels decreased after the procedure (3.3 ± 1.9 vs. 0.8 ± 0.5 mg/dL, P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: Percutaneous tandem MPBS placement is a reversible, metal-free salvage option for duct-to-duct biliary anastomotic strictures after LT. However, 60.4% of patients required additional biliary interventions during follow-up, underscoring the substantial reintervention burden associated with this approach. Its comparative efficacy relative to established alternatives, including biodegradable and removable covered metallic stents, remains undetermined. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Percutaneous tandem modified plastic biliary stenting is a feasible metal-free salvage option for post-transplant anastomotic strictures when endoscopic treatment fails or is unfeasible. Further studies are needed to establish its efficacy relative to biodegradable and removable covered metallic stents.

Color Doppler Ultrasound in Hair Transplant Planning for Cicatricial Alopecia.
articles.abstract: Hair transplantation (HT) has become an important reconstructive option for selected patients with stable cicatricial alopecia. However, objective methods for assessing recipient-site suitability before surgery remain limited. The objective of the study is to describe the structural and vascular ultrasound findings in patients with cicatricial alopecia undergoing preoperative evaluation for HT. This retrospective observational study included 22 patients with cicatricial alopecia evaluated with high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) and color Doppler between 2014 and 2025. Structural variables included dermal and subcutaneous thickness, follicular characteristics, and follicular diameter, while vascular assessment included Doppler patterns and peak systolic velocity. HFUS consistently demonstrated dermal thinning, reduced or absent subcutaneous adipose tissue, and decreased or absent follicular structures. Eleven patients underwent HT, of whom 4 required recipient-site optimization with autologous fat grafting before follicular unit excision. All 4 demonstrated preoperative dermal thickness <3 mm and reduced or absent subcutaneous adipose tissue on ultrasound. At 12 months, graft survival exceeded 90% in 8 patients and was approximately 80% in 3 patients. Limitations: Retrospective design, limited sample size, and clinical heterogeneity. In conclusion, HFUS and color Doppler provide objective assessment of recipient-site characteristics and may support preoperative planning by identifying patients who could benefit from recipient-site optimization before HT.

Noninvasive Prediction of Tumor Malignancy Grade in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma with Dual-Energy CT: A Novel Index Integrating Histopathological Differentiation and Ki-67.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To preliminarily develop and validate an integrated model based on clinical features and rapid-kVp-switching dual-energy CT (DECT) 3D volumetric parameters for the noninvasive prediction of a novel Grade of Malignancy (GOM) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC)-a composite index integrating histopathological differentiation and Ki-67 index. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 183 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC. Patients were randomly allocated into training (n=128) and validation (n=55) cohorts. From the portal venous phase scans, three quantitative 3D volumetric parameters were extracted from the tumor volume: iodine concentration (IC), the slope of the spectral attenuation curve, and effective atomic number. Independent predictors for the GOM were identified through univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis. The discriminatory performance of the developed models was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and clinical utility was assessed with decision curve analysis. RESULTS: The integrated model, which combined the DECT parameter (3D VOI-IC) and CA125, demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to models using clinical or DECT features alone. In the training cohort, the integrated model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.743-0.899), which was robustly validated with an AUC of 0.806 (95% CI: 0.684-0.928) in the validation cohort. Decision curve analysis confirmed that this combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that an integrated model incorporating the 3D volumetric parameter IC from DECT and CA125 could be a useful and noninvasive adjunct for preoperative prediction of the comprehensive GOM in PDAC, though further validation is needed.
